Jackie, the California bald eagle who became an internet sensation, died from illness on Monday, weeks after being injured in an attack by two other eagles, officials announced.

For more than a decade, nature lovers watched via an online video feed as Jackie and her partner Shadow tended to their nest each year atop trees near Big Bear Lake in the San Bernardino Mountains east of Los Angeles.

The nonprofit Friends of Big Bear Valley installed the nest camera in 2015 and documented the successes and failures of each breeding season. In 2024, Jackie diligently sat on her eggs for more than two and a half days straight after a winter storm blanketed the nest with snow.

The Los Angeles County Department of Parks and Recreation’s San Dimas Raptor Rescue team found Jackie on July 17 following reports that the bird had been involved in a fight with two other eagles and was found to be ill.

Jackie had been receiving medical treatment for three weeks at the Ojai Raptor Center, where she was treated for a variety of ailments including anemia. Despite undergoing a blood transfusion and oxygen therapy, her condition worsened and the center announced the animal's death Monday.

Jackie the bald eagle has died after mystery illness

“We know this news will be deeply felt by the many thousands of people around the world who have followed her journey, hoped alongside us, prayed for her, and supported the people caring for her,” the center's statement said. “Our team is heartbroken. It has been an extraordinary privilege to care for her.”

The California Department of Fish and Wildlife is caring for the remains.

Among those who enjoyed monitoring Jackie's nests from afar was biologist Kelly Sorenson, executive director of the Ventana Wildlife Society in central California. While his group was not involved with the Big Bear eagles, he sees their breeding as emblematic of the comeback the species has made in the state over the past decades.

American bald eagles teetered on the brink of extinction until the pesticide DDT was banned in the 1970s and other protections were established, leading the species to rebound and be removed from the federal endangered list.

“You want to see a success story like that,” Sorenson said Monday. “Having access to a live cam to see the nesting first hand is very powerful. It brings people in on an emotional level.”

The Associated Press contributed to this article.

President Donald Trump appeared to zone out during an Oval Office announcement on vaccines, prompting a fresh round of mockery online.

On Monday, Trump signed an executive order that calls for reducing the number of vaccines recommended for children and splitting the MMR shot — which protects against measles, mumps and rubella — into three individual vaccines.

The order is the latest step in the administration’s campaign to remake the childhood vaccination schedule, led by Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who has long questioned vaccine safety.

During the ceremony, the 80-year-old president appeared to repeatedly close his eyes while seated behind the Resolute Desk — including as Kennedy and National Institutes of Health Director Jay Bhattacharya spoke beside him.

Videos of the moments quickly circulated on social media.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump appeared to zone out during a vaccine announcement in the Oval Office on Monday with HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr ( AFP via Getty Images )

“I love how he pops out of it for a few seconds then closes his eyes again and he's right back in dream land. This is getting ridiculous,” wrote one X user. Another chimed in: “Why doesn't the assembled media speak out about this...they all see it.”

“What a loser,” a third user wrote. “After years of listening to those ‘sleepy joe’ comments…” The remark referred to Trump’s longtime nickname for former President Joe Biden, whom he repeatedly accused of being mentally and physically unfit for office.

Some commenters, however, were more supportive of the president. “In Trump's defense, good Lord, the speaker is boring,” one wrote.

The White House defended Trump, saying: “President Trump’s sharpness, unmatched energy, and historic accessibility stand in stark contrast to what we saw during the last administration when Democrats and the legacy media intentionally covered up Joe Biden’s serious mental and physical decline from the American people. President Trump is the sharpest and most accessible President in American history who is working nonstop to solve problems and deliver on his promises.”

Trump, the oldest person ever inaugurated as president, has faced persistent scrutiny over his health since returning to the White House, including over moments during official events in which he has appeared to close his eyes for extended periods. One such moment came during Lindsey Graham’s funeral last month.

“The president has severe daytime somnolence,” CNN medical analyst Dr. Jonathan Reiner said in May. “He falls asleep very often. He’s fallen asleep in the Oval Office on multiple occasions with people talking to him, in the cabinet room,” he said. “And chronic insomnia is a severe illness. It can result in an increase in risk of dementia, a decrease in cognitive effects in older people.”

open image in gallery Director of the National Institutes of Health Jay Bhattacharya (L) speaks before President Donald Trump signs an executive order calling for more research and flexibility on vaccines ( AFP via Getty Images )

Trump, for his part, has repeatedly insisted that he is in excellent health. After a physical at Walter Reed in May, the president wrote on Truth Social that “everything” had “checked out PERFECTLY.”

In a YouGov survey conducted last year, 78 percent of respondents said they believed Trump had not been transparent about his physical health.

The Independent has contacted the White House for comment.

MAGA firebrand Rep. Lauren Boebert’s eldest son, Tyler, has been arrested on child exploitation charges.

The Colorado Republican’s 21-year-old son has faced public scrutiny for several years amid multiple run-ins with the law, including past allegations of child abuse relating to his young son.

On Sunday, the Garfield County Sheriff’s Office arrested Tyler, from New Castle, for sexual exploitation of a child and other charges. The sheriff’s office didn’t specify what the charges were related to in a Monday Facebook post, but said he made a $10,000 bond the day of his arrest.

“I love my son. We take these allegations very seriously and pray for everyone affected during this challenging time,” Boebert told The Independent in reaction to the new charges.

Tyler is the oldest of four sons that the Republican shares with ex-husband Jayson Boebert.

open image in gallery Congresswoman Lauren Boebert’s eldest son, Tyler, 21, is facing a new round of child exploitation charges ( Garfield County Sheriff's Office )

The new charges were first reported by the political watchdog group American Muckrakers.

Tyler was charged with sexual exploitation of a child, induce/entice; sexual exploitation of a child, possession with intent; sexual exploitation of a child, video and two counts of contributing to the delinquency of a minor, multiple outlets reported, citing court records filed Thursday.

The alleged offenses began in January 2024, when Tyler was 18. His next court appearance is scheduled for August 19.

Tyler has already been accused of child abuse twice, once in July 2025 and again this past February.

open image in gallery The Congresswoman’s 21-year-old son has been accused of child abuse in the past, relating to his young son ( Getty Images )

On July 11, 2025, Tyler was cited by the Windsor Police Department on a misdemeanor charge of child abuse, Westword, a Denver-based independent news site, reported at the time.

Boebert told Westword that the citation stems from “a miscommunication on monitoring my young grandson that recently led to him getting out of our house.”

Tyler, whose son was born in June 2023, has been “doing a great job getting his life on track as a father and citizen over the past year,” the congresswoman said in her 2025 statement.

“As the citation states, there was absolutely no injury or physical abuse involved,” Boebert said, adding that Child Protective Services met with her family “to ensure we are continuing to provide a safe environment for my boys and my grandson.”

“I am confident this is a one-time incident that we have addressed as a family,” she added.

open image in gallery 'We take these allegations very seriously and pray for everyone affected during this challenging time,' Boebert said in reaction to the new charges ( Getty Images )

On February 15 this year, Tyler was cited on a misdemeanor charge of child abuse without injury again, 9News reported, citing Windsor Police.

Boebert told the local outlet at the time that Tyler was watching his son at her home while she was at an event in her district and the toddler got out of the house.

"A kind woman quickly and safely secured him, and authorities were called as a precaution," Boebert said, adding that there’s “no excuse” for the incident and that she’s “very frustrated” it happened.

A first responder has accused Andy Burnham’s government of “spitting in the faces of police officers” after Downing Street claimed it cannot stop the early release of two of PC Andrew Harper’s killers.

Former officer Chris Bushnell, who met with PC Harper on the day he died while responding to a quad bike theft in Berkshire in 2019, said he finds the possibility of Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers being released early “absolutely outrageous”.

Downing Street faces immense backlash over the situation, with more than 880,000 people signing a petition calling for the pair to remain in jail, while Thames Valley Police Federation is weighing legal action to prevent their release.

On Monday night, PC Harper’s “really angry” mother Debbie Adlam told ITV News she had not heard from the prime minister: “My message is that you want to tour the country, you want to meet the people. You haven’t even got in touch with me. How about coming to see me?”

Newlywed PC Harper, 28, was caught in a strap attached to the back of a car and dragged down a country road as three teenage suspects fled the scene of the burglary. Mr Bushnell, then a police constable, was waiting in a lay-by for the suspects’ vehicle when he saw it dragging his colleague’s body behind.

The officer pursued but was ordered to stop through the radio. Minutes later, he was told PC Harper had been killed.

In a statement issued through the Thames Valley Police Federation (TVPF), Mr Bushnell said: “I will never get over it. The guilt. That feeling of ‘what if?’ Today, I feel pretty much how I felt the day after it happened.

“This news about the sentencing – and the offenders being released early – has brought it all back again.”

open image in gallery Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers will be eligible for release from January under current plans ( Thames Valley Police )

Cole and Bowers were convicted of manslaughter in 2020. But under current early release plans, they remain eligible to be freed in January – halfway through their 13-year sentences. The driver of the vehicle, Henry Long, received a 16-year sentence and would not be eligible for early release.

Some 5,000 inmates are expected to be released early under sentencing changes, down from 6,000 after the exemptions announced as part of an urgent review of the scheme.

Despite growing pressure, Downing Street said yesterday it is “not possible” to exempt “one or two offenders” convicted of manslaughter from early release.

No 10 insisted Mr Burnham is “far from accepting the situation” but played down the prospect of a carve-out to keep Cole and Bowers behind bars.

“He understands the public wants him to go further, and he wanted to go further, but on the wider issue that prisons would have run out of space, police would stop making arrests, it would be impossible to lock up convicted offenders and that would put public safety at untold risk,” the prime minister’s spokesperson said.

But late on Monday night Sky News reported, via a spokesperson at No 10, that Mr Burnham has asked justice secretary Alex Norris to “work through further options to keep a greater number of the most serious offenders in prison, including the killers of PC Harper”, conflicting with Downing Street’s position throughout the day.

Mr Bushnell, who was serving in the West Berkshire dog unit when PC Harper was killed, said: “I’ve seen people die before. I’ve seen suicides. This was beyond brutal. It was awful.”

Recounting the court hearings he had to attend, Mr Bushnell said: “They were mocking it. The second time they were in the cells, but we heard they weren’t even paying attention.

open image in gallery Pc Harper, 28, was caught in a strap attached to the back of a car and dragged down a country road as three teenage suspects fled the scene of the burglary ( PA Media )

“There was no remorse at all. It was almost a joke to them. Nothing serious. If you have an accident, if you kill someone, you show remorse. I just can’t comprehend it.

“And for all this to be coming up again now is unbelievable. It stirs up all those emotions once more.”

Mr Bushnell, who retired from Thames Valley Police in 2022, added: “We can’t change the verdict. They got their sentences, which were pretty pitiful, to be fair.

“When I first heard a couple of weeks ago there was a chance they could be let out early, I was shaking. It brought everything back.

“To think they could be released early is absolutely outrageous. I’m angry with them, but I’m also angry with the government. They’re spitting in the face of police officers.”

“They have got to serve their full sentence. Andy did his duty that night. The least they can do is show him some respect.”

The national chair of the Prison Officers’ Association, Mark Fairhurst, said he is “positive we could free up additional space and block anybody convicted of manslaughter from early release”.

He added: “You only have to look at the remand population. We’re knocking on to some 17,000 people on remand. I’m sure we could get a couple of thousands of them bailed or tagged with the GPS tag to monitor them electronically. That’s an easy win for this government and I can’t understand why they don’t consider it.”

open image in gallery Andy Burnham is facing mounting backlash over the early release scheme ( PA Wire )

It comes despite Mr Burnham earlier this week saying he had “pushed to the very limits of what is possible to do without risking the prison system reaching capacity and collapsing” by excluding sentences for “rape, serious child sex offences and other grooming offences” from eligibility.

Reforms in the Sentencing Act came after prisons came close to running out of space entirely last year, risking the “total breakdown of law and order”, which would leave police unable to make arrests and courts unable to send offenders to custody, the then justice secretary Shabana Mahmood said.

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said: “The death of PC Andrew Harper was a horrific crime. Our thoughts are with his family and friends, and we share the anger from the police community that we are in this position.

“Thanks to tireless campaigning by Andrew’s family, Harper’s Law means that anyone convicted of killing an emergency worker whilst committing a crime now gets a mandatory life sentence. This government has gone further by introducing a presumption that anyone convicted of murdering a police, prison or probation officer is handed a whole-life order.

“We have been clear that we wanted to go further and block more offenders from getting out sooner into their sentence but could not do so without risking prisons reaching capacity and collapsing.

“If that happened, police could not make arrests, courts could not remand offenders and there would be unchecked criminality on our streets.”

Sitting in her car one morning before work, Sabrina Javellana was frantically scrolling through photos of herself online that someone anonymously sent her a link to, with an ominous warning of their explicit content.

As she sifted through the dozens of images, posted on 4chan, she came across one that made her freeze.

“I recognized one from when I was 17 in high school, just taking a cute picture in a mirror of my outfit, about to go hang out with my friends…except my clothes were totally removed,” she recalled.

“It was the same exact photo, except they used this AI-generated technology to remove my clothes, and it looked hyper-realistic. But I knew this wasn't real. From that day on, my world turned upside down.”

Javellana was 23, working in local politics in Florida, when she fell victim to AI deepfake pornography in 2021, which she describes as an act of sexual violence.

open image in gallery Sabrina Javellana was 23 and working in local politics when she fell victim to AI deepfake pornography in 2021. She said it turned her life ‘upside down’ ( Sabrina Javellana/Getty )

With the unstoppable rise of AI technology, it has never been easier for perpetrators to create and share nonconsensual sexually explicit deepfakes. The estimated number of deepfakes rose from approximately 500,000 in 2023 to 8 million in 2025, according to analysis. And 99 percent of deepfakes target women.

Still, it remains unclear how serious tech bosses are about tackling the problem. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman appeared unaware of the latest deepfake bill being pushed by lawmakers on both sides of the aisle when The Independent quizzed him on it in Washington, D.C. recently, while Elon Musk’s xAI is suing Minnesota over its attempts to ban so-called “nudification” apps in the state.

Momentum to tackle nonconsensual sexually explicit deepfakes by the U.S. government had been picking up steam after Congress passed the TAKE IT DOWN Act last year. It prohibits the publication of authentic and AI-generated sexual images published without a person’s consent, and requires online platforms to remove them within 48 hours of a complaint.

The DEFIANCE Act would allow victims to file civil lawsuits against people who produce, distribute, and solicit nonconsensual deepfake AI pornography, as well as those who intend to distribute such images.

It was cleared the Senate by unanimous consent in January but is languishing in the House, with time running out. The bipartisan bill, introduced by New York Democratic Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and co-sponsored by Republican Rep. Laurel Lee of Florida.

But some Republicans, it seems, do not want to hand Ocasio-Cortez a win so close to the midterms in November, when she is up for election.

When The Independent recently asked Ocasio-Cortez about the GOP lawmakers reportedly blocking the bill because her name is attached to it, her response was blunt. “I don't think that we should be emboldening child pornographers and helping abusers just because of some personal beef that they may have,” she said.

open image in gallery Paris Hilton told The Independent: ‘Every day the DEFIANCE Act isn’t put on the calendar in the House, more women and girls become victims without a meaningful path to justice’ ( Getty Images )

Ocasio-Cortez said that she would welcome the assistance of first lady Melania Trump, who supported the TAKE IT DOWN Act.

“I think that this is a really great opportunity, just as we have in the House, to be able to champion and for women to uplift one another across party lines,” she told The Independent.

Javellana said the issue transcends party politics and described the blockage as “petty.”

“It feels like a slap in the face to the women and girls who have spoken so bravely to tell their stories,” Javellana, 28, told The Independent. “This is not about making AOC's star even brighter.”

At a January press conference, Ocasio-Cortez teamed up with Paris Hilton, where the pair spoke of what it feels like to be a victim of deepfake AI pornography. Hilton said that more than 100,000 deepfake images of her exist online and has urged lawmakers to pass the DEFIANCE Act.

“Every day the DEFIANCE Act isn’t put on the calendar in the House, more women and girls become victims without a meaningful path to justice,” Hilton exclusively told The Independent.

I felt fear for my family, my home. It impacted my stress, my health, everything. It crushed me to step away, but I had to for my sanity, for my survival, for my health, for my safety Sabrina Javellana

Hilton added that there is “no legitimate policy reason” for the bill to be stalled and hit out at Rep. Jim Jordan, Chairman of the House Judiciary Committee. “Representative Jim Jordan and House leadership have an opportunity to protect millions and send a clear message that people who knowingly create or distribute nonconsensual explicit deepfakes to cause harm will be held accountable,” Hilton said.

Jordan’s office did not respond to a request for comment.

As AI technology advances at pace, the law is yet to catch up on holding perpetrators and Big Tech accountable for sexually explicit deepfakes and other online harms. And while the DEFIANCE Act “isn’t perfect,” Javellana said, introducing civil penalties provides victims with “more tools in the toolbox.”

In 2018, then aged 21, Javellana became one of the youngest elected officials in Florida when she won a seat on the Hallandale Beach city commission in Broward County, located between Miami and Fort Lauderdale. The young politician threw herself into issues she cares about deeply, which her critics deemed progressive.

“I'm speaking about climate change, I'm speaking about police reform, I'm speaking about government corruption,” she said.

open image in gallery Javellana suffered in silence for a year, not wanting to tell her family or friends about the images. After speaking out, she has joined advocates like Paris Hilton to call for legislation to stop AI deepfake pornography ( Getty Images for The Ford Founda )

The online abuse soon followed. “Because I was outspoken, because I was a young woman and an easy target,” Javellana said.

Everything changed on the day she received the first AI deepfake, depicting her nude. More popped up, and still do to this day, she said. “It’s not just the photos, but the comments from all these anonymous users. I would do her, I would rape her... just disgusting, vulgar comments.”

She served her four years in office but decided not to run for re-election following the ordeal.

“I felt fear for my family, my home,” she said. “It impacted my stress, my health, everything. It crushed me to step away, but I had to for my sanity, for my survival, for my health, for my safety.”

She had limited options for recourse but reached out to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement and consulted with a New York-based attorney. Due to a lack of state and federal legislation about AI deepfakes at the time, neither resulted in any morsel of justice. It was baffling to Javellana that what happened to her did not constitute a crime.

“It wasn't illegal to do this to people, to take their own likeness and make it into a new nude image and put their face on it and destroy their life, their career,” she said. “I totally lost my sense of self. I felt like I had no agency over my own body…I felt like this was a new form of sexual violence.”

open image in gallery Hilton has hit out at Republican leadership for stalling on the bill. ‘Representative Jim Jordan and House leadership have an opportunity to protect millions and send a clear message that people who knowingly create or distribute nonconsensual explicit deepfakes to cause harm will be held accountable,’ she said ( Getty Images )

Javellana suffered in silence for a year, not wanting to tell her family or friends about the images.

“It felt like a losing battle,” she said. “I decided maybe no one will ever see these. I'll never talk about it to anyone. I'll just, you know, compartmentalize it and try to move on with my life.”

Then, in January 2022, then-Florida Democratic state senator Lauren Book introduced a bill making it a felony to create sexually explicit deepfakes without consent. Book went public with her own experience where she was blackmailed with sexually explicit deepfake AI images.

Javellana reached out to Book to share her story and testified about her ordeal in the Florida Senate, marking the beginning of her public fight for women and girls. “I reached out to [Book’s] office and I told her, ‘Hey, this happened to me, and I want to help support your bill and make sure it gets passed.’”

With Javellana’s help, the Florida bill was swiftly signed into law by Governor Ron DeSantis. She hopes the DEFIANCE Act will follow suit, stressing that federal lawmakers can’t afford to delay.

open image in gallery First lady Melania Trump supported the TAKE IT DOWN Act last year, which prohibits the publication of authentic and AI-generated sexual images published without a person’s consent, and requires online platforms to remove them within 48 hours of a complaint ( Getty Images )

Prince Harry and Meghan are the latest high-profile names to back the bill. The couple criticized House lawmakers given the bill has been passed by the Senate.

“This begs the question: why the delay?” a release last week from the Duke and Duchess of Sussex asked. “The answer may lie in the deepest offense to families and children: the tech industry’s commitment to pushback on these bills to protect their bottom line.”

It isn’t only high-profile women and girls who are being targeted, as instances of deepfakes are cropping up more and more in schools, an issue Hilton has also raised.

“Around 99 percent of nonconsensual explicit deepfakes target women. But anyone can become a victim,” she told The Independent. “These AI tools and nudification apps are becoming cheaper, faster, and easier to use. All it takes is a single photo, and within seconds a coworker, stranger, classmate, or ex-partner can create realistic explicit images that can devastate someone’s reputation, career, relationships, and mental health.”

Javellana added: “Big tech has started this revolution where it's growing so fast, our laws are not catching up to it. It's going to continue to grow, impacting women and girls in all different aspects of life, not just public figures, politicians, celebrities. It's impacting more and more every single day, [including] girls in school.”

The bill is flailing even though it enjoys the support of House Speaker Mike Johnson as well as right-wing firebrands like GOP Reps. Nancy Mace of South Carolina and Anna Paulina Luna of Florida, in addition to progressive Democrats like Reps. Jamie Raskin of Maryland and Ro Khanna of California.

It has not so much as come up for a vote in the Judiciary Committee - which handles legislation relating to legal affairs and votes on whether to put a bill on the House floor - which is galling to many survivors.

open image in gallery The DEFIANCE Act is flailing in the House and time is running out to pass it. Javellana is calling on lawmakers to get it done ( AFP via Getty Images )

“AOC is a very powerful force, but it's so much bigger than her,” Javellana said. “And I know that these [Republican] leaders see that. It would be a win for them just as much as for her, as for President Trump.”

“This is common sense and to survivors, to victims...it's upsetting.”

But Javellana and other advocates remain confident that the DEFIANCE Act will become law. She is already looking ahead to the next fight.

“We're still not going to be done because this is still very reactive and not preventative,” she said of the bill. “And the preventative is once we start talking big tech, once we start talking about holding the platforms liable.”

“They are not good at all about responding to inquiries and reports of people asking to take this [content] down or regulating their users,” she added.

Indeed, when The Independent asked OpenAI CEO Sam Altman for his take on the DEFIANCE Act last week, he said he was “unfamiliar” with it. This was the same week the entrepreneur was in Washington, D.C., to talk with lawmakers about AI policy.

Javellana doesn’t believe she will ever discover the identities of the people who created the deepfake pornographic images of her, but whatever happens, she won’t be silent anymore.

“I wanted to hide for a while, but you know what? I can't do that,” she said. “That's letting them win.”

If you need support, call the Rainn National Sexual Assault Hotline at 800-656-HOPE (4673) or visit rainn.org

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want
News.content:
Liverpool 2 Monaco 3

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

News.title: Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion
News.content:
Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

Sports.title: Liverpool sign Araujo from Barcelona
Sports.content:
Liverpool have confirmed the signing of defender Ronald Araujo from Barcelona.

The deal is an initial loan for the 27-year-old, who signed a new contract with Barca until 2031 last year, and also includes an option to buy for around £47.14m (€55m).

⁠Liverpool are not paying Barcelona a loan fee and will cover the entirety of Araujo's salary for the duration of the season-long loan. It is understood Araujo has taken a pay cut to facilitate the move.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Liverpool sign Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo on loan with an option to buy.

Araujo, who will wear the No 33 shirt, told Liverpoolfc.com: "I can't wait to get started. I'm very, very happy.

"I'm excited to be here at this massive club with lots of history. I'm excited to meet my team-mates, excited to get started playing, and I'm very motivated and really up for getting going.

"I think it was the ideal move for me at this stage in my career. I think it was a move that was necessary for me to take. As soon as I heard that interest from Liverpool, everything went into action really, really quickly.

"As I say, I'm super-happy to be here and excited to get started. I'm glad about the interest and it was the right move at the right time."

The Uruguay international, who did not play at the World Cup due to injury, is expected to train with his new team-mates this week.

Araujo will add to Andoni Iraola's options at the heart of his defence following the departure of Ibrahima Konate to Real Madrid and fitness concerns over inexperienced 21-year-old Jeremy Jacquet.

Jacquet, a summer signing from Rennes, has made fewer than 100 senior career appearances and has not featured in pre-season yet after missing the second half of last season following shoulder surgery.

Joe Gomez suffered a muscle injury in Liverpool's opening pre-season game, while teenage centre-back Giovanni Leoni is still recovering from an ACL injury, leaving captain Virgil van Dijk as Liverpool's only fully-fit senior centre-back.

Image: Liverpool have signed Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo on a season-long loan

Araujo, who can play at right-back and centre-back, moved from his native Uruguay in 2018 and made his Barcelona debut the following October, going on to play more than 200 games for the LaLiga side.

He was named as one of the club captains following the departure of Marc-Andre ter Stegen in January, but started only 11 LaLiga matches for the Catalan giants last season after an extended break from football in November 2025 to recover from what he later revealed was depression.

Why the Araujo deal works for Liverpool...

Liverpool had not been actively seeking out defensive reinforcements, their priority firmly on adding a wide forward, but this was a market opportunity that made sense for a number of reasons.

Ronald Araujo can play at centre-back or right-back, and, crucially, he was available on loan. This offered an appropriate solution to injury concerns that are deemed to be more short-term.

Liverpool have already committed £60m to signing Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes, with a view to him partnering Virgil van Dijk at centre-back.

However, it remains to be seen if he will be fit for the start of the season, as Liverpool take caution with his re-integration to competitive action following a shoulder injury that has kept him out since February.

A muscle problem for Joe Gomez, which will keep him out for the Premier League opener against Newcastle, has worsened the problem for new head coach Andoni Iraola, who by his own admission is slim on options at the back.

Araujo arriving on a temporary move alleviates that injury headache and adds a layer of experience to Liverpool's backline that is sorely missing. He has played more than 200 games for Barcelona after all.

There are understandable concerns around whether Araujo can turn around his struggles with form and fitness. Liverpool are not short on defenders with patchy injury records.

Liverpool are taking on a deal with an element of risk in that regard. But there is also a potentially big reward if Araujo does rediscover his best form thanks to the option to buy inserted in the deal worth around £47m.

At the peak of his powers, Araujo was being valued at around double that figure. Liverpool will hope to see his best in the Premier League, a division which is seemingly suited to his strengths.

How Liverpool were able to get Araujo

This is a deal that suits all parties. Liverpool require defensive cover amid injury worries around a number of players, while Araujo is not part of Hansi Flick's plans at Barcelona and is in need of a fresh start.

Araujo signed a new contract with Barcelona last year in January that reportedly put him among the club's highest earners. Six months earlier, he had been named Barcelona's vice-captain.

However, the Uruguay defender has since been unable to reach the heights that earned him such high status at Barcelona amid struggles with injury and his mental health.

Araujo wore the captain's armband as Barcelona celebrated becoming champions of Spain in May, but he had only played 24 times throughout the season.

Flick admitted when confirming the deal that Araujo was not suited to the way he wants to play and said the defender was excited about having the chance to move to a new environment.

Barcelona can now bring in a defender that Flick wants to work with, and Araujo has the opportunity to rebuild his career in the Premier League. If he performs, they will either earn a decent fee from Liverpool or his value will increase.

Sports.title: Sciver-Brunt helps Trent Rockets Women into Hundred final
Sports.content:
England all-rounder Nat Sciver-Brunt timed her introduction to perfection as 32 off 19 balls batting down the order secured Trent Rockets' progress to the final of The Hundred with a seventh successive victory.

Chasing 118 to win, the league leaders slipped to 10-3 against Southern Brave, the lowest powerplay score in the history of the competition, and even though passing 27 guaranteed their place in the final, the result remained in doubt.

Sciver-Brunt came in at number seven with the score on 66-5 and with 31 deliveries remaining - Ash Gardner having top-scored with 37 - and her experience avoided further drama.

She was run out going for a second which would have clinched victory, but Rockets still won with two balls to spare.

Southern Brave's 117-5 was built around their top order with Maia Bouchier scoring 38, Lizelle Lee 31 and Laura Woolvaardt adding 24.

They will get a second chance as they had already secured a place in the eliminator on Friday at The Kia Oval. Brave will discover their opponents on Tuesday, who will either be third-placed SunRisers Leeds or fourth-placed Manchester Super Giants who play each other at Emirates Old Trafford in their final group match.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Georgia Adams was run out in unfortunate fashion after Sarah Glenn fumbled a drive from Nat Sciver-Brunt and deflected the ball on to the stumps

Sciver-Brunt said: "I'm happy to be on the winning side. The wicket was a bit slow, and they bowled pretty well in the first half."

On batting down the order, she said: "It was a bit tactical and a bit injury management. We have got a lot of people in form and high on confidence. We have balanced our side nicely and building up to Sunday we sort of know what we need to do."

Sports.title: Rangers meeting Q&A: McInnes-Klopp compared, club failure admission & new signings update
Sports.content:
Rangers chairman Andrew Cavanagh believes the Ibrox side have become used to finishing second or worse over the last 15 years, and admits that failure had begun to "seep through" every corner of the club.

He was speaking at the club's shareholders' meeting, where it was also revealed they expect to add three to five more players this window, while Derek McInnes' appointment was compared to that of former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp.

It was also confirmed that Rangers have asked for an explanation over Hibernian's penalty in Sunday's 2-1 defeat as refereeing concerns were raised.

Image: Jim Gillespie was appointed Rangers chief executive in January

Chairman Andrew Cavenagh, Paraag Marathe of the San Francisco 49ers [who are part of the US consortium who took over the club], executive director Fraser Thornton and chief executive officer Jim Gillespie addressed a number of club issues and answered questions from the floor.

Here are some of the key takeaways...

On Derek McInnes

Image: Derek McInnes left Hearts to take charge of Rangers this summer

During the meeting, one shareholder asked why Derek McInnes, the man they wanted to ask questions to after a winless start to the season, was absent. Andrew Cavenagh explained that the panel had been arranged months ago and that McInnes' focus was at the training ground to help prepare the team.

When asked later about the process behind hiring McInnes, Jim Gillespie said you can either hire a 'Klopp' or a 'Guardiola' type. He said McInnes fitted the 'Klopp' type of being a manager who wants his teams to be agressive, on the front foot and attack the opposition.

During the summer when McInnes was appointed, Sky Sports News revealed he was the only candidate who was spoken to, and Gillespie defended that by adding he was the only option Ibrox chiefs felt "ticked all the boxes".

Cavenagh reminded shareholders that "culture eats strategy for breakfast", and when speaking about standards, revealed people had been late to training and not eating well. He went on to say he believed McInnes was the right man to address this.

On Recruitment

Image: Daisuke Yokota is one of nine summer signings at Rangers so far

Multiple shareholders raised concerns about player recruitment. However, Cavenagh defended the work in that department, adding he believes the squad is better than it was 12 months ago.

He admitted the team still requires between three and five more players before the end of the transfer window.

The meeting was called following a £16m share issue. Cavenagh confirmed that was needed to get the club through this "significant" summer transfer window. He added the club "will need more capital going forward".

Marathe insisted that they were "building something special" and referenced Youssef Chermiti's performances in the second half of last season, after initially struggling with the pressure of his price tag and playing for Rangers.

Image: Youssef Chermiti was injured in Sunday's defeat to Hibs, hours after it was revealed a bid had been rejected for the striker

On Chermiti, the club hierarchy were asked why he was selected for Sunday's match against Hibernian despite being the subject of a bid from Galatasaray. The striker was subsequently stretched off injured in the first half of that defeat.

It was explained that to accept a bid, Rangers need their value of the player to be met, and for sufficient time to reinvest those funds in the squad to make it equal or better. They reiterated there is no pressure to sell.

On Refereeing standards

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hibernian were awarded a first-half penalty in their 2-1 win at Rangers

Gillespie said that Rangers should be a leading club and want to have a constructive relationship with the Scottish FA and SPFL, while also holding both to account.

He was interrupted by a shareholder who said: "It's not working. It's been going on for years, nothing happens."

Marathe replied: "You're not wrong" but backed up Gillespie by saying, "we can't make it worse, we can't be in any more of what feels like a disadvantage".

Marathe added "he couldn't believe" the decision to award Hibernian a penalty in the first half of Sunday's match at Ibrox. Gillespie confirmed that Rangers have made contact with the Scottish FA to seek an explanation.

On Ibrox stadium

Image: Ibrox could be redeveloped with several proposals being considered

Marathe - who has overseen stadium expansion at Leeds United and the 49ers - discussed possible changes at Ibrox.

He said there would be news on that soon, while revealing one proposal is to lower the pitch at Ibrox, adding 5,000 to 6,000 seats.

It was also revealed, following fan surveys, a number of other ideas have been through a feasibility group and seen by architects.

Call for unity

Sports.title: Chelsea get Luton as Spurs to host Charlton in Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
Chelsea will host Jack Wilshere's Luton Town in the Carabao Cup second round, while Tottenham Hotspur host Charlton Athletic in a London derby.

Former Arsenal midfielder Wilshere will take his League One outfit to Stamford Bridge, as the 11 Premier League sides not involved in European competition this season joined the winners of the first-round ties in the hat.

Among the other tasty ties are League One AFC Wimbledon visiting Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham at Craven Cottage, while Keith Andrews' Brentford face a potentially tricky tie against Birmingham at St Andrew's.

Plymouth - who won the Devon derby with Exeter, live on Sky Sports on Monday night - will get Premier League side Coventry City at home, while West Ham face an all-Championship tie away to Southampton.

In the north draw, Newcastle have been given Championship side West Brom at home, while Leeds were given an all-Premier League clash against Nottingham Forest.

David Moyes' Everton go to second tier club Preston - as the Toffees boss reunites with the club where he began his managerial career.

Like the first round, the second round draw was also regionalised and split into Southern and Northern section ties. The second-round matches will be played in the week commencing August 24.

The remaining Premier League teams will join in the third round, which will be split over the week commencing September 7 and the week commencing September 14. The teams competing in the Champions League will start in the later week.

Sports.title: Donald Trump says it would be a ‘terrible mistake’ to replace Fifa’s Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
US president Donald Trump has warned Fifa would be making a “terrible mistake” if they get rid of Gianni Infantino as the head of world football’s governing body.

Infantino has come under pressure following his doomed plan to sell off stakes in the men’s World Cup to private investors.

But in a post on his Truth Social social media site early on Tuesday, Trump said removing the Fifa president would be a costly move.

The US president wrote: “Fifa would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing president Gianni Infantino.

“He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented. If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!”

Uefa and two other confederations have held initial talks about organising competitions themselves amid the backlash against the embattled Fifa president.

Europe’s governing body, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and Concacaf, which oversees football in the ‌Caribbean, North and Central America, have accused Infantino of “deception” and while it is understood they want to give him the chance to resign and leave his position with dignity without seeking re-election in March next year, they want to insulate themselves from the unfolding crisis.

Uefa has previously threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions.

Infantino apologised for his proposal to create Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), a company to run the commercial and operational aspects of Fifa’s tournaments, with an idea to sell off around 20% to private investors.

But an open letter signed by the heads of Uefa, AFC and Concacaf has urged Fifa to hold an independent review into Infantino’s scheme, while not naming the Swiss directly.

“Leadership in football is not a possession,” the letter said. “It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held. It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it.

“When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.”

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 3: Bournemouth
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 12th (NB: this is not necessarily Ben Fisher’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 6th

Prospects

It was the day after the final game of last season at Bournemouth’s secluded, swish training base and, before clearing his belongings on his last day in the building, the departing head coach, Andoni Iraola, spent a couple of hours in his office chewing the fat with his successor, Marco Rose, talking players, pubs and tactics. The story goes that, with time moving on, Tiago Pinto, the club’s sporting director, knocked on the door to advise them there were other things to tackle.

It was an interesting scenario that speaks volumes of the respect between the pair. Long before joining Bournemouth, Iraola cited Rose’s Borussia Mönchengladbach side as one of his favourite teams to watch, the German’s “vertical football” helping them qualify for the Champions League in Rose’s first season in charge.

Rose accepts that Iraola, in absorbing the sales of key players totalling more than £250m last season and qualifying for Europe for the first time, has set a high bar. Remarkably, Bournemouth did not lose a game after the sale of Antoine Semenyo in the second week of January. Rose put it succinctly during pre-season in Austria. “Andoni didn’t leave a lot of space to improve,” he said. “Pressure’s on.”

In his first session, Rose told the players he loved the way they attacked the Premier League last season. Playing in the Europa League, however, represents uncharted territory for a team in the second tier as recently as four years ago. It is why Bournemouth’s hierarchy contacted peers at Crystal Palace and Nottingham Forest to understand the realities of juggling the Thursday-Sunday rhythm the competition will bring. Rose is close friends with Oliver Glasner, who is now at Forest, but won the Conference League last season with Palace. “We are not going to Europe just to enjoy, we want to be competitive,” Rose said. “We are not there just to watch.”

Unlike last summer, so far they have retained all key players, chiefly Alex Scott, Rayan and Eli Junior Kroupi, the 20-year-old forward who breezed into double figures in his debut Premier League season and the club consider a generational talent. Kroupi attracted serious interest from Paris Saint-Germain, among other European superpowers, but a freak foot injury during a pre-season drill means he is sidelined for at least three months.

At the end of the season, Bournemouth earmarked a centre-back to replace Marcos Senesi and a striker to compete with Evanilson as key priorities and by the start of August the club had recruited Álvaro Rodríguez, whom Rose wanted to sign at Leipzig, and António Silva from Elche and Benfica respectively. Juanlu Sánchez joined from Sevilla to provide competition for Adam Smith, the evergreen 35-year-old into his 14th season at the club, and will also fill the void left by Álex Jiménez, who has joined Fiorentina on loan with an option to sign permanently because he remains suspended in England while under investigation by the Football Association.

Off-field picture

The smallest stadium in the Premier League has been a building site this summer, with the club working to ensure their 11,357-seater ground complies with Uefa regulations. There has been a wider facelift, too, with every seat being replaced, while they are filling in two corners to increase the capacity by 800 this season. Playing in Europe brings the challenge of meeting Uefa’s squad-cost ratio (SCR) rules, which caps on-pitch spending at 70% of a club’s revenue. Bournemouth finished the 2025-26 season at 82% and they continue to work towards meeting the threshold. Last month the academy was awarded category one status, four years after being category three.

Owner-fan relationship

The American billionaire Bill Foley described himself as a dictator upon buying the club approaching four years ago, but supporters are grateful for his naked ambition. Foley, who made his fortune in insurance, is forthright and somewhat prophetic. In 2023, he said the club would play in Europe within five years – and achieved it in three. It was a similar story with Vegas Golden Knights, whom he vowed would win the Stanley Cup within six years of him launching the ice hockey franchise in 2017 – they won it in their sixth season. Foley recently added rugby union’s Exeter Chiefs to his sporting stable, which extends to Lorient, Auckland FC and Moreirense. Not every decision is universally popular but Foley, who turns 82 in December and predominantly splits his time between California and Vegas, puts his money where his mouth is.

The manager

As a defender, Marco Rose was schooled by Jürgen Klopp and Thomas Tuchel at Mainz, and Ralf Rangnick at Hannover, so had quite the education before beginning his coaching career at home town club Lokomotive Leipzig. Klopp told Rose, after promotion to the Bundesliga in 2004, that he would excel in the dugout and he has since managed some of the biggest names: Erling Haaland and Jude Bellingham at Borussia Dortmund, Dominik Szoboszlai and Dani Olmo at RB Leipzig. Rose has been compared to Klopp and, naturally, Iraola, given his appetite for high-energy tactics. Bournemouth routed Genoa 10-1 in pre-season so, could his style be even more aggressive than Iraola’s? “I would say [to be] even more aggressive than Andoni is quite difficult,” came the reply. His grandfather, Walter Rose, represented Germany in 1937.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen António Silva has all the attributes to be a bargain buy for Bournemouth. Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty Images

These days, £50m is about the going rate for an elite defender. Tottenham paid £52m to sign Jan Paul van Hecke. Chelsea paid the same fee to take Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace. Bournemouth pocketed £50m when Dean Huijsen joined Real Madrid last year, though that price was set by a release clause. They are deals that make Bournemouth’s £25.7m purchase of António Silva, a 22-year-old who has been a regular at Benfica since breaking into the team and has experience in the Champions League, Europa League and 20 caps for Portugal, appear a snip. Silva, who is right-footed but prefers to play as a left-centre back, is a direct replacement for Senesi.

Stat attack

Bournemouth scored nine goals from Opta-defined counterattacks last season, the joint most in the Premier League. But their threat was varied; in only two of their preceding eight top-flight campaigns did they score more set-piece goals than the 14 they managed in 2025-26. It is very rare for a team to be so productive on both fronts.

Set for a breakthrough

It was a November night of ecstasy when Scotland qualified for the World Cup for the first time in 28 years, but for Ben Gannon-Doak it was a bittersweet evening and one that curtailed his club season. The 20-year-old was forced off after 21 minutes, replaced by Kenny McLean who capped the scoring in style. A £25m arrival from Liverpool last August, Gannon-Doak featured in all three of Scotland’s World Cup matches, starting the first and last, and has impressed in pre-season. After being limited to 113 minutes in eight league appearances as a substitute last campaign, there is optimism Gannon-Doak will make his mark.

World Cup impact

Rayan became the first Brazilian teenager to start a World Cup match since Marco Antônio in 1970 when he was named in Carlo Ancelotti’s starting XI for their Group C game against Scotland. The then 19-year-old, signed from Vasco de Gama in January, set up Vinícius Júnior for Brazil’s opener in the 3-0 win and afterwards swapped shirts with Gannon-Doak. Tyler Adams enhanced his reputation, impressing for the USA en route to the last 16. Two new members of Bournemouth’s coaching staff, the set-piece coach, Nicolas Gagnon, and goalkeeping coach, Frederic de Boever, worked with Canada and Belgium respectively. Alex Scott’s inclusion in Tuchel’s pre-World Cup training camp in Florida spoke volumes of the Guernsey-born midfielder’s wider standing.

Sports.title: Liverpool owners close to £1.35bn sale of 30% stake to consortium including Jeff Bezos
Sports.content:
A consortium including the Amazon founder, Jeff Bezos, is close to completing a deal for a 30% stake in Liverpool after months of talks with Fenway Sports Group. The investors are led by Amit Bhatia, the son-in-law of the Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal and who previously was a shareholder and director at Queens Park Rangers.

The Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin is another member of the group who will pay in the region of £1.35bn. The deal is effectively agreed, but may take up to a month to complete.

Bezos has a personal fortune of around $257bn (£190bn), according to Forbes, making him the fourth-richest person in the world, while Saverin is reportedly worth $32bn. This will be Bezos’s first investment in football, but he has previously looked into bidding for NFL franchises. The 62-year-old will receive equity as part of the deal, which Deloitte has advised on.

Bezos is the executive chair of Amazon having relinquished day-to-day control when he stepped down as chief executive five years ago. Under his leadership, the online retailer has diversified into being an entertainment provider and has bought numerous sports rights for its streaming service.

Amazon had live UK rights for 20 Premier League games each season for six seasons until the end of last year and broadcasts the Champions League in several European countries, as well as some NFL games in the US.

FSG bought Liverpool in 2010 and have overseen two Premier League titles. FSG sold 3% of the club to the US private equity firm Dynasty Equity in 2023.

It has been a summer of change at Anfield, with Andoni Iraola replacing Arne Slot as head coach, Mohamed Salah left on a free transfer and has joined Trabzonspor and Michael Edwards departed his role as chief executive officer at FSG.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest owner Marinakis sues Crystal Palace over fan banner
Sports.content:
The Nottingham Forest owner, Evangelos Marinakis, is suing Crystal Palace for defamation after supporters of the south London club displayed a banner depicting him holding a gun to the head of the England midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White.

Almost 12 months since the banner appeared midway through the first half of Palace’s 1-1 draw with Forest at Selhurst Park, lawyers for Marinakis lodged the claim for defamation against CPFC Ltd and “persons unknown” at the high court on Monday.

The banner showed the Greek shipping magnate pointing the gun at Gibbs-White, who had been set to join Tottenham last summer before Forest pulled out of the deal, and also featured the message: “Mr Marinakis is not involved in blackmail, match‑fixing, drug trafficking or corruption.” Marinakis has previously rejected all those allegations. Lawyers for Marinakis were approached for comment. A spokesperson for Palace did not comment.

Palace were fined £50,000 by the Football Association in February after being found guilty of failing “to ensure its spectators and/or supporters (and anyone purporting to be supporters or followers) didn’t behave in an improper, offensive, abusive, insulting and/or provocative way at this match”. The FA added in its statement: “The fact that Crystal Palace had a policy to prevent banners being smuggled into the stadium demonstrates that it was aware of the risk.”

Last summer, Palace and Forest were at loggerheads after Forest wrote to Uefa to voice their concerns that Palace could be in breach of multiclub ownership rules. The FA Cup winners ended up being demoted to the Conference League, with Forest – who had finished seventh in the Premier League and originally qualified for the Conference League – promoted in their place. Palace went on to win that competition under Oliver Glasner, while Forest reached the Europa League semi-finals.

Glasner has since joined Forest after leaving Palace at the end of his contract in a move that has surprised both sets of supporters. The Austrian said this week that Marinakis had persuaded him to change his mind over dinner in Athens after previously rejecting Forest because they were not in Europe next season.

“Then I had a more detailed look and there are two reasons why I changed my mind and I told him,” Glasner said. “No 1 is I think there is more potential in the squad than they have shown. And No 2 is you, it’s your ambition, because I am very ambitious.”

Sports.title: Are Manchester United returning to relevance under Michael Carrick? | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Manchester United finally seem to have something that resembles stability in the dressing room under Michael Carrick. I feel with quality signings in defence and midfield, they could mount a decent challenge for the Premier League next season. How do you feel they will fare? – Sterling.

There’s an odd sense that Michael Carrick’s level of achievement last season was at precisely the most awkward level for the board. United didn’t produce indisputably brilliant football under him but equally 12 wins and three draws in 17 games was good enough that they pretty much had to give him the job. But it’s one thing to turn out those kinds of results when the pressure’s off, you’re already out of both cup competitions and you don’t have any European football; it’s quite another to do it in the heat of a full season. United don’t have to have an especially amazing season to play 15 more games this season than they did in 2025-26.

That’s not to say that Carrick won’t be successful. There was much that he did last season that was very impressive. Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans bolster an area of the squad that desperately needed to improve. A left-back seems almost certain to arrive before the end of the month and there’s probably the need for one more high-class experienced central defender. It’s not clear what Marcus Rashford’s future is after his return from loan at Barcelona, but he has two years left on his contract and could add dynamism and finishing to the left side of the attack. It’s probably not a title-winning squad, but it’s certainly one that should qualify for the Champions League.

Two questions remain that will only be answered as the season goes on. First, Carrick himself: can he cope with the churn of two games a week, and operating with a squad that is at least as fatigued as their opponents? And second, where is the club psychologically? Part of the problem for United, a familiar trait of big clubs who have fallen from grace, is that they have got into a routine of failure, that no success can ever quite be trusted, and every setback is seen as a further example of the terminal decline (although just as damaging would be suddenly believing everything is fine if United were to win, say, their first three games of the season). Retaining clarity of thought and making realistic assessments are perhaps the greatest challenges for a club that has known greatness but is struggling to return to those heights.

What do you see the broader impact of the VAR changes that Fifa made this year being? Do you think that other soccer leagues will see the increasingly automated, faster but less human approach taken by Fifa this summer and choose to adopt it? (I am aware that the Premier League has already chosen to reject much of it) – Dennis.

The most notable changes implemented before the World Cup allowed VAR to review and overturn incorrectly awarded corner kicks, certain attacking fouls and clear mistakes relating to red cards given from a second yellow. The only one of these adopted by the Premier League is to allow VAR to overturn a second yellow leading to a red (VAR cannot recommend that a referee should award a second yellow that would lead to a red). If we have to have VAR, that seems reasonable enough; nobody wants to see a team incorrectly reduced to 10 men.

At the World Cup, the corner issue only rarely came up, but it always seemed slightly odd that incorrectly awarded goal kicks could not be turned into corners. Personally, I would scrap VAR, or at least this form of it, but if incorrect decisions can be corrected quickly and unobtrusively then they probably should be. I understand, though, why the Premier League, aiming for a “light touch” – good luck with that – would be resistant.

Greater use of VAR, though, seemed to be the direction of travel. I suspect relatively soon offsides will be almost fully automated, which probably makes sense so long as it’s almost instantaneous. Whatever doubts there may be about margins of error and frame rates, it’s still going to be more accurate than a 40-year-old running the line 30 yards away, peering through a thicket of players.

More significant is probably the Premier League’s adoption of regulations against timewasting: speeded-up substitutions, players who receive treatment having to remain off the field for 60 rather than 30 seconds, an outfield player having to be withdrawn for 60 seconds after a goalkeeper receives treatment, and a five-second clock on throw-ins and goal kicks. All should speed up the game and improve the spectacle. It’ll be interesting as well to see the level of tolerance for grappling in the box, particularly by attacking players, which was an area in which the Premier League seemed out of step with the rest of Europe last season.

Which of the Premier League’s promoted sides have the best chance of staying up, and why? – Nicholas.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The achievements of Sunderland and Leeds last season, finishing seventh and 14th, will have heartened the promoted sides, but the truth is it will be extremely difficult for all three. Both those sides invested heavily in a way that is impossible for Coventry, Ipswich or Hull. It’s very hard to see how Hull, who were promoted unexpectedly, can survive. Coventry, perhaps, with the euphoria of their Premier League return and the Frank Lampard factor can give it a go, but their summer spending has been modest. Ipswich, with recent Premier League experience, have a chance and have made some intriguing signings in Daizen Maeda, Abdul Fatawu, Issa Diop and Chuba Akpom, but they’ve lost the manager who got them up, with Kieran McKenna opting for a break rather than another Premier League campaign. Gary O’Neil perhaps feels he has unfinished business, but if any of the promoted sides are to survive, they need another club to have a dreadful campaign.

Sports.title: Carabao Cup second-round draw: Chelsea host Luton, Forest at home to Leeds
Sports.content:
Five-time winners Chelsea have been handed a home draw against League One Luton in the second round of the Carabao Cup. Chelsea’s new manager, Xabi Alonso, will begin the club’s attempt to win the competition for the first time since 2015 later this month.

Fellow Premier League side Tottenham have also benefited from a home draw, against Championship opponents Charlton. The 11 top-tier sides not involved in European competition enter the draw in the second round, with the remaining nine following in round three.

Fulham host League One AFC Wimbledon, Brentford have a potentially tricky away day at second-tier Birmingham while Ipswich host Leicester. Also in the southern section West Ham, who beat Portsmouth in Saturday’s first round, travel to Championship side Southampton.
