Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

In the northern section, the headline fixture features last season’s Europa League semi-finalists Nottingham Forest hosting fellow top-flight opposition in Leeds.

The new Newcastle head coach, Matthias Jaissle, has been given a home draw against West Brom while the Everton manager, David Moyes, will return to Preston, where he was a player and manager. Premier League newcomers Hull travel to Stoke.

Plymouth will host Coventry, who won the Championship title last season, after stoppage-time goals from Alex Hartridge and Bim Pepple gave them a 2-0 win over Devon rivals Exeter.

Ties are scheduled to be played in the week commencing 24 August. The 2026-27 final is on 21 March at Wembley.

Sports.title: Jordan Nobbs ready to complete wishlist with Newcastle WSL dream
Sports.content:
Jordan Nobbs says winning promotion to the Women’s Super League with Newcastle would fulfil her ambition for a north‑east club to be in the top tier.

Nobbs, who has 71 England caps, was born in Stockton‑on‑Tees and believes women’s football in the region would benefit immensely from top‑flight representation. Newcastle finished sixth in WSL2 last season, 11 points behind the title winners, Birmingham, and nine points off the playoffs, but this summer they have made their hopes clear with high-calibre signings from the top division, including the striker Martha Thomas from Tottenham and the Liverpool duo Leanne Kiernan and Gemma Evans.

Nobbs is clear about the target for the new campaign. “It is promotion. I know we said it last season [too],” she said. “I’ve always said things don’t happen overnight, [but] that is our goal. You have to say it out loud.

“Looking back on last season, we had some really good performances but nine draws, that’s too many points [dropped]. It’s just about focusing on finding a way to win. We’ve just got to build on the good stuff from last season, I don’t think we’re far off it.

“[Winning promotion with Newcastle], I’ve always said it would be job done. I think to get a northern team promoted … as I heard from Newcastle I was like, that is exactly what I want to do. In the WSL, I’d ticked as much as I possibly could, so to get a north‑east team, which we all had to leave back in the day, promoted would be an achievement I would love.”

Nobbs began her career with Sunderland and broke into their team in the old top flight, but moved to Arsenal when the WSL was launched in 2011 and Sunderland’s application to join the breakaway division was rejected. That led to a successful team also including Nobbs’s future England teammates Lucy Bronze and Lucy Staniforth breaking up.

Sunderland did compete in the top tier between 2015 and 2018, but north-east representation in the WSL has been sparse, so Nobbs is pleased to see investment in recent years at Newcastle as well as their WSL2 rivals, who were taken over in June by Bay Collective.

“It’s been a long time coming, but it was something us northerners have always wanted,” Nobbs said. “We don’t want the north-east to fizzle out. We want to show the players that have come from there and developed there.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“It’s definitely grown in the right direction now, which is what we wanted. But the big stepping stone would be getting into the WSL. That would be where we really put the north-east back on the map and I’d love to be a part of that.”

The 33-year-old has enjoyed her role in Tanya Oxtoby’s setup at Newcastle after joining them last July. “With Villa I played a lot of a deeper role and [now] I really love being back in my high position, scoring goals, assisting and [I’m] in my happy place. I feel like I found that little spark again [last season] that was nice.”

Sports.title: Manchester City closing in on £85m Bouaddi to soften blow of Rodri’s expected exit
Sports.content:
Manchester City are closing in on signing Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille, with the midfielder’s expected arrival clearing the path for Rodri to join Barcelona. The 18-year-old has agreed personal terms with City, but the club are still finalising the deal with Lille who value Bouaddi at €100m (£85m).

City’s new manager, Enzo Maresca, wants to integrate the Morocco international into his first-team squad immediately. City meet Arsenal in the Community Shield on Sunday and start their Premier League campaign against Bournemouth on 23 August.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Barcelona are confident of signing Rodri from City, but they will have to return with an improved offer after an initial €45m bid was rejected last week. The sale of Ferran Torres, who is of interest to Paris Saint‑Germain, would finance Rodri’s purchase. City are all but resigned to the sale of the 30‑year‑old, who has a year left on his contract.

If the Bouaddi deal can be completed, he would join Elliot Anderson, who arrived last month from Nottingham Forest for £116m, in a new-look midfield, which has lost the experience of Bernardo Silva.

Manchester United, meanwhile, are interested in the Leicester player Louis Page. United, who face competition from Arsenal, are hopeful of securing a deal for the 18-year-old midfielder, with Page believed to favour a transfer to Old Trafford.

Marcus Rashford has joined United at their County Kildare training camp following the England forward’s post‑World Cup break. The 28-year-old has spent the past season and a half on loan at Barcelona and Aston Villa respectively, in the aftermath of a breakdown in his relationship with the club executive and the former United head coach Ruben Amorim. Relations have now eased and Rashford is focused on working under the United manager, Michael Carrick, although he could still leave before the end of the transfer window.

Sports.title: Jason Cundy stuns talkSPORT hosts as he storms into studio before making huge Chelsea statement
Sports.content:
Jason Cundy stuns talkSPORT hosts as he storms into studio before making huge Chelsea statement

Jason Cundy is back from his holiday, and he's come steaming in to tell the world that the Premier League title is Chelsea's this season.

The huge Chelsea fan and former player has been away from talkSPORT Towers since the World Cup, but his first appearance back hosting The Sports Bar saw him go out on a limb.

4 Cundy is backing the club he loves to spoil Arsenal's Premier League title defence

He's backing his beloved Blues to end their ten-year wait for a title, citing a 'cheat code' that they have on their rivals.

Cundy backs Chelsea to win Premier League

“I’m going to make a statement now. There is no reason why Chelsea cannot win this title. In fact, I’m going to say it. Chelsea will win the title," Cundy said on Monday night's Sports Bar.

“There is something about Chelsea. We have got a cheat code. I’m not proud of it but we can win the title for a number of reasons.

“Have you seen our front three? Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer - Palmer’s had a rest, Joao Pedro’s had a rest.

“Our midfield, the recruitment at the back. It almost certainly looks like we could be playing three at the back with someone in Xabi Alonso who knows how to win a title.

“One game a week, we saw how beneficial that could be when Antonio Conte came in, went to three at the back. Win the title.

“History is going to repeat itself. I never go out on a limb when I talk about Chelsea but I said Arsenal will win it for the last three seasons and eventually they did.

“Gooners, you should be fearful of Chelsea. Yes, you’re favourites, I get it. You’ve got an unbelievable team.

“But I’ve got to tell you there’s a cheat code and that’s Chelsea playing one game a week and a manager in Xabi Alonso who knows how to win a title.

“There are only two managers in this league that have won a title - Xabi Alonso and Mikel Arteta. Liverpool, new manager. Andoni Iraola doesn’t know how to win a title.

4 Chelsea boss Alonso guided Bayer Leverkusen to Bundesliga glory for the first time ever in the 2023/24 season, the team going unbeaten for the entire league season Credit: AFP

“De Zerbi at Spurs, what’s he won? Carrick, what’s he won?"

Cundy admitted he still has reservations about Robert Sanchez still being Chelsea's first choice goalkeeper, before putting those worries to one side and bellowing: “CHELSEA win the Premier League title.”

The Blues have bought well and spent a lot of money, with Morgan Rogers the standout recruit following his British record transfer from Aston Villa to add another attacking option.

Veteran Premier League stars Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson bring experience, while the defence is being bolstered as well.

Marco Palestra and Maxence Lacroix have both made the move to west London.

Full-back Palestra made the £47million move from Atalanta, while Lacroix will offer proven quality following his arrival from Crystal Palace in a deal worth £52million.

4 Alonso comes with pedigree and he's been backed in the transfer window, signing Rogers on a British record deal Credit: Getty

Cundy unveils new look

Earlier in the evening, Cundy made an appearance on Transfer Insiders, where he copped a dig from hosts Flex and Abbi Summer for being away for so long.

And that prompted Cundy to storm into the studio and take a seat, although it was his transformation with his barnet following a hair transplant that blew Summers and Flex away.

As he walked in, Flex said: "Who is this? It's a new man. You look incredible. I am being deadly serious

Clearly chuffed with the results, Cundy responded: "It's nuts, isn't it. It's got body and a little lift."

Sports.title: Every Premier League club ranked as final 2026/27 league table predicted
Sports.content:
The most open and unpredictable Premier League season is almost upon us as another season of twists and turns awaits.

Champions Arsenal unofficially kick off the season against FA Cup winners Manchester City in the Community Shield, live on talkSPORT.

9 Will it be Arsenal and Man City going head-to-head for the title once more? Credit: Getty

The two teams finished first and second in the table last year and are many neutrals' pick to duke it out for the title again in 2026/27.

However, City are among the nine of the 20 top-flight teams that will begin the new campaign with a different manager.

The World Cup has also wreaked havoc on many clubs' pre-season plans, with some stars reporting to training late and others carrying varying degrees of injuries.

It's also important not to hold too much stock in friendly results: Liverpool lost three such matches in the summer of 2019 ahead of winning 26 of their first 27 league games en route to lifting the title.

Arsenal, meanwhile, have just lost back-to-back fixtures this month - but remain the bookies' favourite to defend their crown come May.

With that in mind, here is where all 20 sides rank in talkSPORT's predicted Premier League standings (insert apology for your respective team's position here).

Arsenal

The Gunners held off a spirited challenge from Man City to win the club's first Premier League title in 22 years last season.

Mikel Arteta may have missed out on a few key targets since then, most notably Vinicius Junior extending his stay at Real Madrid.

But, Arsenal have signed one of the best Premier League midfielders in Newcastle skipper Bruno Guimaraes.

And, with the exception of Leandro Trossard, they have also kept the core of the squad widely regarded as the deepest in the division.

With the added experience from both manager and players in how to get over the line, Arsenal remain the favourites to defend their title.

talkSPORT Prediction: 1st

9 Arsenal will be preparing for a title-defending campaign Credit: Getty

Aston Villa

Unai Emery has worked miracles at Villa Park since his arrival and again overperformed last season to finish fourth.

The Spaniard has since seen stars plucked from his ranks once more, with Morgan Rogers completing a £117million move to Chelsea, while Manchester United snapped up Youri Tielemans for £35m.

Set-piece coach Austin MacPhee has also departed the club, with Ezri Konsa the latest to be linked with the exit door.

The arrival of Alejandro Garnacho has done little to inspire fans, and considering Villa slipped to sixth the last time they were in the Champions League, it looks an uphill battle for Emery once again.

talkSPORT Prediction: 7th

9 Unai Emery has lost a number of key players this summer Credit: Getty

Bournemouth

The Cherries will play in Europe this season for the first time in their history after going on an epic 18-game unbeaten run in manager Andoni Iraola's final few months.

The Spaniard has since taken the reins at Liverpool, with Marco Rose tasked with juggling Europa League commitments this campaign.

In Bournemouth's defence, they have still not even lost a Premier League game since January and have resisted the mass exodus of their stars this summer that has plagued the club in recent years.

But Eli Junior Kroupi will be missing for months after undergoing surgery, and the extra fixtures coupled with a manager new to English football suggest the south-coast outfit could struggle.

talkSPORT Prediction: 14th

Brentford

Keith Andrews surprised all the critics who tipped the Bees for relegation last season by masterminding a European push.

Brentford ultimately fell short of a historic campaign by finishing ninth, and it could prove to be a massive case of what if for the club - with Jordan Henderson also ripping up his contract to join Chelsea.

Their alarming dip in form at the end of last season can't be ignored either - with their only win in their final 10 Premier League games from the start of March coming against relegated West Ham.

Igor Thiago also scored over 40 per cent of the Bees' 55 goals, the highest per cent any individual contributed to one term in 2025/26.

Brentford have never had a player score over 20 Premier League goals in multiple seasons, and a drop in his output could prove hugely damaging for Andrews' side - with back-up Callum Wilson only managing seven in the top-flight last year.

talkSPORT Prediction: 17th

9 Brentford won just one of their final 10 Premier League games Credit: Getty

Brighton

The Seagulls boasted the seventh best home record in the Premier League last season en route to qualifying for Europe in eighth.

Yet Brighton proved their issues coping on two fronts in 2023/24, when their Europa League adventures saw them finish 11th.

And it might prove to be a similar story for Fabian Hurzeler's men this season, despite the coup signing of Luka Vuskovic from Tottenham, replacing Jan Paul van Hecke, who moved to Spurs in a separate deal.

But Brighton have lost Danny Welbeck after the best goalscoring return of his career, with long-time servants Adam Webster and Solly March exiting on free transfers and James Milner retiring.

talkSPORT Prediction: 11th

Chelsea

The Blues will have ambitions of being the league's dark horses despite finishing out of Europe for the second time in six years.

Antonio Conte won the title in 2016/17 with no European football, with Mauricio Pochettino also improving the team by six places and 19 points from 12th in 2022/23 in similar circumstances.

Xabi Alonso has been backed heavily, with a transfer record for a British player spent on Rogers alongside £52m for Maxence Lacroix.

Crucially, Chelsea now also have several experienced heads in the dressing room in English pair Henderson and Welbeck, similar to how Alonso utilised Granit Xhaka and Robert Andrich in his dominant Bayer Leverkusen side.

However, World Cup winner Marc Cucurella officially departed Stamford Bridge in June, and it seems a tall ask for a developing team to instantly challenge for the top honours - securing Champions League football should be the main aim.

talkSPORT Prediction: 4th

9 Chelsea have completed the £117million signing of Morgan Rogers this summer Credit: Getty

Coventry City

Frank Lampard will always have credit in the bank with the Sky Blue faithful after ending their 25-year wait to regain top-flight status.

Club captain Matt Grimes even told talkSPORT that the Chelsea legend is one of the world's best coaches.

However, the omens are far from ideal - only in four of the Premier League's 31 seasons have the three relegation spots not been occupied by a promoted club.

And Lampard's recent record as a Premier League manager doesn't read pretty - a win percentage of just 27.27 per cent at Everton, while he won only one of his 11 games during his second Chelsea stint.

Coventry have also had a relatively quiet window, while it remains to be seen whether the trio of Haji Wright, Brandon Thomas-Asante and Ellis Simms can replicate their Championship goal-scoring feats at the top level.

talkSPORT Prediction: 19th

Crystal Palace

The Eagles have had the best two seasons in their history with FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League glory.

But Palace may find themselves going backwards this year, with star defender Lacroix following manager Oliver Glasner out the door.

Splashing what was briefly a club record £35m on Brennan Johnson in January only to swap him for Dwight McNeil half a year later doesn't evoke a heap of confidence from the Palace hierarchy.

With the added demand of Europa League football this term, new head coach Pierre Sage has had to contend with free transfers to shape his squad in Oscar Mingueza and Takehiro Tomiyasu.

Sage was sacked by Lyon halfway into his only managerial season juggling European football, and with Palace fans expecting another positive showing on the continent after last year, it could come at the cost of improving on their 15th-placed Premier League finish.

talkSPORT Prediction: 15th

Everton

Toffees fan and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has boldly predicted his beloved team to finish seventh.

Yet it's hard to forget Everton's dismal end to last season, which had them in the relegation zone from April 11th to their final game - as one of only three teams without a Premier League win in that spell alongside relegated Wolves and Burnley.

David Moyes has put a lot of trust in youngsters Tyrique George and Hayden Hackney to take to regular Premier League football quickly.

Iliman Ndiaye is in talks to join Al Hilal, while the bulk of the goalscoring burden will fall again to Beto and Thierno Barry - who have both never reached double figures in the Premier League.

talkSPORT Prediction: 13th

9 Everton were just three points off the Champions League places with seven games left last season but then imploded Credit: Getty

Fulham

Alvaro Arbeloa has already been tipped to be the first Premier League manager sacked this season before his first official game.

The Cottagers have even been tipped for relegation by talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor, such is the risk they've taken in appointing the Spaniard as Marco Silva's successor.

Arbeloa has just five months of senior managerial experience to his name and has spent the bulk of the club's transfer kitty on two youthful Real Madrid starlets in Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios.

Meanwhile, Fulham have lost their two leading scorers from last season with Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez departing as free agents; Alex Iwobi, in third, only managed four Premier League goals.

talkSPORT Prediction: 16th

Hull City

The Championship Play-Off final winners have so far only spent money on goalkeepers Jack Butland and Konstantinos Tzolakis.

Hull owner Acun Ilicali was bullish on talkSPORT about his side's chances of staying up, but a mixture of inexperience and the overall squad's quality make them heavy favourites to go back down.

The Tigers haven't played in the Premier League since 2017, and manager Sergej Jakirovic has never led a team at this level.

Sunderland, in similar circumstances this time last summer, became the fourth-highest-spending promoted club ever - which means Hull will need something pretty spectacular to give themselves a chance.

talkSPORT Prediction: 20th

Ipswich Town

talkSPORT.com is sadly predicting a return to the successive 2023/24 and 2024/25 seasons that saw all three promoted clubs relegated.

That latter campaign involved Ipswich, who returned to the Championship in 19th, and that recent experience might just be enough to stand the club in a better stead than Coventry and Hull.

The Tractor Boys have a new boss in Gary O'Neil following the departure of promotion-winning manager Kieran McKenna.

Abdul Fatawu, Daizen Maeda, and Issa Diop are all eye-catching signings to make a stab at survival, but the overall quality of the squad will likely still see them finish in the bottom three come May.

talkSPORT Prediction: 18th

9 Ipswich celebrated wildly by booking their place back in the top-flight Credit: Getty

Leeds United

Daniel Farke's side have plenty of reasons to believe that the possibility of replicating Leeds' ninth-placed finish in 2021 is in reach.

Having consolidated their place in the Premier League last season in 14th, the club then beat out plenty of competition to pick up Wilson.

The Welsh international scored 10 goals and assisted seven more last term, with Leeds also showing their intent by landing Tarik Muharemovic after his impressive showings in Serie A and breaking their transfer record to make James Trafford their new No.1.

All this points to the fact that simply avoiding relegation again is no longer the goal for the Whites: a top-half finish is more than possible.

talkSPORT Prediction: 9th

Liverpool

The Reds had a dismal season last year after finishing in fifth spot in the table - 25 points behind champions Arsenal - despite a record-breaking £446million splurge.

Arne Slot was sacked, and Andoni Iraola is the man tasked with bridging the gap and will need plenty of help in the market to do so - namely in a potential double transfer raid on Paris Saint-Germain for wingers Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.

There is no Mohamed Salah, who has joined Trabzonspor on a free transfer, but Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz both need and are expected to have far greater second seasons at Anfield.

Isak remains one of the world's best strikers - with injuries restricting him to just three goals in 14 Premier League outings last term - and an uninterrupted pre-season could see him reignite a squad who are just 14 months removed from winning the title.

Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo has been loaned as an emergency defensive reinforcement, but Iraola is still in dire need of further depth at both ends of the pitch, and failure to act before the window shuts could mean the difference between a title challenge or another fight to secure a European spot.

talkSPORT Prediction: 2nd

9 Isak managed just four goals in all competitions last season Credit: Getty

Manchester City

Pep Guardiola’s 10-year reign at the Etihad is over, and his former assistant Enzo Maresca has incredibly large shoes to fill as new head coach.

Bernardo Silva, John Stones, and Nathan Ake have all left a sizable hole of experience and leadership in the dressing room.

But the biggest miss will undoubtedly be the expected exit of irreplaceable Rodri to either Barcelona or Real Madrid.

The Spaniard, who won the Ballon d'Or in 2024, claimed the Golden Ball at the 2026 World Cup, and £116m man Elliot Anderson will instantly be under massive pressure to shoulder the midfield burden.

Last season's Golden Boot winner Erling Haaland will be sure to fire City into the title conversation whatever the makeup of Maresca's side looks like, but it does ultimately feel to be a season of transition.

talkSPORT Prediction: 3rd

Manchester United

Michael Carrick impressed after fixing the mess left behind by Ruben Amorim to guide the Red Devils to a third-place finish.

Yet the 45-year-old has been left very short in a bid to challenge on multiple fronts after qualifying for the Champions League.

United refused to engage in bidding wars for Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, with the club also beaten by City for Anderson.

Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans are shrewd midfield signings, but that area remains light after Casemiro's exit, and Manuel Ugarte, who is a long-term absentee through injury, with Mason Mount as well having a suspect fitness record.

Man United jumping from 15th to third in one year shows the value of not playing in Europe - and with that benefit going to two of the club's biggest rivals for a Champions League place in Chelsea and Spurs, it could be a major cause of concern if further recruitment isn't made.

talkSPORT Prediction: 5th

9 Michael Carrick is gearing up for his first full season as Manchester United manager Credit: Getty

Newcastle

The Toon Army may have had the summer from hell on paper, but there is plenty for fans to remain optimistic about.

Former club captain Guimaraes has departed to join Arsenal in a £75m deal to follow fellow high-profile players Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon in leaving for pastures new.

But the squad had grown stale under former boss Eddie Howe, and Matthias Jaissle has an opportunity to start the rebuild job at Newcastle in a season where fans won't be expecting much.

There is hope that Yoanne Wissa can take his World Cup form into his second season at St James' Park under Jaissle's favourable system.

The Magpies additionally won't have the added strain of playing in Europe this year, with a top-half finish and a cup run both reasonable expectations.

talkSPORT Prediction: 10th

Nottingham Forest

Forest are coming off a chaotic campaign that featured four managerial changes, a relegation battle, and a run to the Europa League semi-finals.

The arrival of Oliver Glasner as head coach is not only a major coup, but a chance for the club to enjoy some much-needed stability.

The loss of Anderson is undoubtedly a blow, but the overall squad assembled by Evangelos Marinakis was always more representative of one who finished seventh in 2024/25 than 16th last season.

Spearheaded by Morgan Gibbs-White, who bagged 18 goals in all competitions, Glasner will be itching to prove he can translate his success in cup competitions to the league.

talkSPORT Prediction: 8th

Sunderland

Regis Le Bris' men bucked all recent trends for Premier League promoted sides by qualifying for the Europa League last season.

But shocking the world for a second time will be an extremely tall order, with the squad looking very much the same as last campaign.

Sunderland did manage to keep signing of the season, Granit Xhaka, out of Chelsea's clutches, while adding Thomas Meunier's experience.

The demands of consistent Thursday/Sunday football on the Black Cats will take its toll on any domestic ambitions - with a comfortable finish away from a relegation fight enough for fans to really savour those European trips.

talkSPORT Prediction: 12th

Tottenham

Spurs have endured successive 17th-placed finishes in the Premier League, but there is genuine cause to hope brighter times are ahead.

For one, the Lilywhites have been the biggest spenders so far, splashing out nearly £250m, and they are not done yet.

The north London outfit have also broken their transfer record twice to revamp their midfield in the capture of Fernandes and Tonali.

Roberto De Zerbi won't have the extra demands of European football in his first full season at the helm, and he's demonstrated the impact he can make during his short stint in charge of Tottenham.

The issue for Spurs remains the lack of an elite goalscorer, with Richarlison their top scorer in all competitions last year with just 12 goals.

talkSPORT Prediction: 6th

Sports.title: Diego Poyet, son of ex-Tottenham and Chelsea star Gus, looks unrecognisable with arms like Thor
Sports.content:
Diego Poyet, son of ex-Tottenham and Chelsea star Gus, looks unrecognisable with arms like Thor

Ex-West Ham midfielder Diego Poyet showcased a radically different look to his playing days in a recent Instagram post.

The 31-year-old is the son of former Tottenham and Chelsea hero Gus Poyet, and enjoyed a football career of his own before retiring in 2020.



3 Fans will remember Poyet boasting long curly hair during his time at West Ham Credit: Getty

The younger Poyet rose through the youth ranks at Charlton, before breaking into their first team in 2014.

He went on to make 23 senior appearances that season, winning the club's Player of the Year before joining West Ham in the summer that followed.

Poyet would ultimately feature just three times for the Hammers after making his Premier League debut in August 2014.



The tenacious midfielder had loan spells at Huddersfield, MK Dons and Charlton during his time with the east London side.

Following his release, Poyet moved to Argentina to play for Godoy Cruz and then joined Cyprus outfit Pafos, before leaving in 2018 and later calling time on his career after two years without a club.



Muscle machine

A few things have changed in the years since his retirement from football, with Poyet finding a new love for working out.

And the former Uruguay youth international now looks completely unrecognisable from his playing days, boasting a ripped physique.



Back in 2022, Poyet revealed his body transformation with a series of Instagram posts showcasing his bulked-up physique and short hair - a world away from his days as a slim, long-haired footballer.

And he has clearly kept up his fitness regime since then, which he revealed in a recent social media post.

Taking to Instagram, Poyet shared a picture of himself with a shaved head and grown out beard, and still boasting an impressive bodybuilder physique.

3 The former midfielder looks radically different to the slender build he had as a player Credit: Getty



Father and son duo

As well as committing to a disciplined new lifestyle in the gym, Poyet has also remained involved in football since his retirement.

With father Gus being appointed manager of the Greece national team in 2022, Diego joined him in the dugout as assistant manager.

This continued two years later, as Diego then teamed up with his Premier League icon father when he took charge of South Korean side Jeonbuk Hyundai Motors in 2024.

And while Poyet Junior has been looking to emulate Senior as a coach, Gus revealed their lifestyles are radically different as he gave an insight into his son's rigid gym routine in 2023.



Discussing Diego's body transformation, Gus said: “From what I understand, because I’m not a specialist, is he’s 100 per cent in everything that he does - to the top.

“For example, we went to dinner one day and people will have a beer or a glass of wine - no chance. He doesn’t touch alcohol. Never.

3 Gus Poyet had his son as part of his backroom team during his two years as Greece manager Credit: Getty

“We finished dinner and we put three or four desserts in the middle; proper, proper desserts. I love them, but he doesn’t touch them.



“So his way of behaving, what his aim is, he’s 100 per cent, he’s not 99 per cent. His way of training, knowing when he needs to grow, when he needs to slim down, when he needs to do a kind of diet, it’s all proper."

Sports.title: Chelsea, Tottenham and Newcastle learn Carabao Cup opponents as Tom Brady’s Birmingham host Premier League side
Sports.content:
Chelsea and Tottenham just about managed to avoid each other in the Carabao Cup second round draw.

Spurs take on Charlton in a London derby which will be the first competitive meeting between the two clubs since 2011.



3 The draw for the Carabao Cup second round has been made Credit: Getty

Right before that fixture was drawn, Chelsea were given a showdown at home to League One Luton Town, who are managed by ex-Arsenal star Jack Wilshere.

The match will represent Xabi Alonso's first Carabao Cup tie as manager.

It follows his appointment as the club's new boss earlier this summer.



Meanwhile, 2025 winners Newcastle United host West Brom for a place in the third round.

Birmingham City, part owned by NFL legend Tom Brady, have been handed a Premier League opponent, with the Championship club drawn at home to Brentford.



Blues are two-time winners of the competition, last doing so in 2011.

Their opponents Brentford, meanwhile, have lost to the eventual champions in each of the last two seasons.

The draw for the second round of this season's competition was held on Monday night.



It was conducted ahead of the final opening round tie between Plymouth Argyle and Exeter City at Home Park.

The winner of that match will host Coventry City in the next round.

3 De Zerbi's Spurs narrowly avoided a tie against Chelsea and instead face Charlton Credit: AFP

Carabao Cup details

All 35 first round winners will be joined by the 11 Premier League clubs not playing in Europe.

Those sides in continental action this term will enter in the third round.



As with the first round, the second round is once again split into Northern and Southern sections.

Ties will be played the week commencing August 24, with matches going straight to penalties if they finish level after 90 minutes.

They follow a frantic weekend of first round action across the Football League.

Championship, League One and League Two sides were joined by the two winners from the preliminary round.



3 Alonso will take on Luton in his first Carabao Cup match as Chelsea boss Credit: Getty

Carabao Cup second round draw in full Matches to be played w/c August 24 Northern section: Stoke vs Hull

Newcastle vs West Brom

Blackburn vs Sheffield United

Nottingham Forest vs Leeds

Doncaster vs Middlesbrough

Barnsley vs Crewe

Preston vs Everton

Blackpool vs Lincoln

Sheffield Wednesday vs Wolves

Bradford vs Burnley
