World.title: Armenian Catholicos Garegin II attends first hearing in criminal trial
World.content:
Catholicos of All Armenians appears in court

A court in Armenia‘s Armavir region has begun hearing the criminal case against the Catholicos of All Armenians and six bishops who serve on the Supreme Spiritual Council. Garegin II attended the hearing in person.

Clergy members and politicians gathered outside the courthouse. Lawmakers from the opposition Armenia Alliance and I Have Honour Alliance left parliament during the afternoon and travelled to Etchmiadzin to show their support for the Catholicos. Dozens of worshippers also gathered outside, periodically chanting “Your Holiness” and singing traditional Armenian church hymns (sharakans).

Prosecutors accuse the Catholicos and the senior clergy of obstructing the enforcement of a court ruling.

Garegin II removed Bishop Gevorg Saroyan, head of the Masyatsotn Diocese, from his post. Saroyan is one of the senior clerics who joined Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s campaign to “reform the Church”. The bishop challenged his dismissal in court. The court ordered his temporary reinstatement as head of the diocese until it reaches a final decision in the case. However, before the court could rule on the merits, the Supreme Spiritual Council, led by the Catholicos, also defrocked him. The council argued that the courts have no jurisdiction over the Church’s internal affairs.

Lawyer Ara Zohrabyan says the Catholicos faces criminal prosecution for carrying out his “ecclesiastical and canonical duties”.

He argues that state interference in the Catholicos’s decisions violates the principle of Church autonomy, the constitutional relationship between the state and the Church, and freedom of religion.

“In this criminal case, the court will examine not only the charges against specific individuals, but also another fundamental question: whether the secular authorities can interfere in the internal life of the Church and criminalise the exercise of the canonical authority of the Catholicos of All Armenians,” the lawyer said.

The trial comes after tensions between the government and the Church steadily escalated.

About a year ago, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan called for the Catholicos to step down. He first argued that Garegin II could not lead the Church because he had broken his vow of celibacy and had a daughter. He later accused the Catholicos of having links to foreign intelligence services. The ruling Civil Contract party has also included the removal of the “de facto head of the Church” in its election manifesto.

Members of the ruling party accuse the Church of interfering in Armenia’s domestic and foreign policy. The parliamentary opposition rejects that claim. Opposition lawmakers argue that it is the government that is unlawfully interfering in the Church’s affairs.

First hearing ends after 30 minutes as judge recuses himself

Shortly after the hearing began, Judge Hakob Manukyan announced that part of the proceedings would take place behind closed doors because they would involve “personal information”. He said the information concerned both himself and the Catholicos’s lawyer.

“A few minutes later, lawyer Ara Zohrabyan told journalists: “The judge has recused himself. He has withdrawn from hearing this case.”

According to Zohrabyan, the judge said he had once granted him his licence to practise law, which could “raise doubts about his impartiality”. Zohrabyan said he did not believe this constituted valid grounds for recusal.

“However, he refused to take part in this disgraceful trial. The very fact that the Catholicos is standing trial is deeply troubling. The case will now go to another judge.”

After the hearing, the Catholicos of All Armenians and his supporters headed to the cathedral to attend a church service and pray together.

Garegin II: “The authorities are trying to bring the Church under their control”

After the service, the Catholicos addressed those gathered outside the cathedral. He said the authorities were taking steps to undermine the Church’s authority, restrict its autonomy and bring it under their control.

“The authorities are persecuting the Church and the clergy. They have arrested and restricted the freedom of a number of clergymen, benefactors and other patriotic individuals through unlawful and fabricated criminal cases,” he said.

The Catholicos dismissed the charges against himself and the six clergymen as groundless.

“We remain steadfast in our faith and determination to defend our rights, which are guaranteed both by our country’s Constitution and by the fundamental principles of international law.”

Opposition declares a “day of shame”

Marianna Gakhramanyan, an MP from the opposition I Have Honour Alliance, said:

“Today is a day of shame. The Catholicos of All Armenians, our spiritual father and the head of our Church, is standing trial in Etchmiadzin. It is shameful and unprecedented. This is an attack not only on the independence of the Armenian Apostolic Church but also on Armenia’s Constitution, which clearly states that the political authorities have no right to interfere in the affairs of the Church and that the Church is separate from the state.”

“Who is defending the Church – us or you?” asks ruling party MP

Commenting on opposition lawmakers who came to support the Catholicos, Civil Contract MP Artur Hovhannisyan said:

“The Church has begun interfering in Armenia’s domestic and foreign policy.”

He also referred to the allegations that the Catholicos had violated his vow of celibacy:

“We are the ones standing with the Church. We are the ones defending the Church. You are defending clergymen who broke their vow of celibacy, who engage in politics and use religion and the Church to protect themselves from the consequences of breaking that vow and taking part in politics. Anyone who has broken the vow of celibacy should leave the Church.”

The ruling Civil Contract party’s election manifesto also outlines plans to reform the Church. Under the proposal, the “de facto head of the Church”, as Pashinyan’s team refers to the Catholicos, should leave office. The plan calls for the election of a locum tenens, the adoption of a new Church charter containing “mechanisms to preserve centuries-old traditions”, and, ultimately, the election of a new Catholicos.

Comment

Political analyst Tigran Grigoryan told Reuters:

“Pashinyan has come to see the Church as a political threat and as an institution capable of supporting the opposition and various political parties in their efforts to gain power.

“The case against the clergy fits into a broader pattern of selective justice pursued by Pashinyan’s government, under which leading opposition figures have been arrested and some of their property has been confiscated by the state.”

Catholicos of All Armenians appears in court

World.title: Azerbaijan FM in Kyiv: gas for Ukraine, visit to Irpin, Ukrainian drones
World.content:
Azerbaijani FM visits Ukraine

Azerbaijan‘s Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov paid an official visit to Ukraine on 6 August.

It was the first visit by an Azerbaijani foreign minister to Kyiv since the start of Russia‘s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Bayramov began his visit with a trip to Irpin, where he viewed an exhibition of Ukrainian-made drones and laid a wreath at a memorial to fallen defenders at Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry.

He also held meetings with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, President Volodymyr Zelensky, Head of the Presidential Office Andriy Yermak, Defence Intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov and National Security and Defence Council Secretary Ihor Klymenko.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

One of the most notable announcements was Azerbaijan’s stated willingness to supply Ukraine with natural gas if needed.

The two sides also discussed the possible use of Ukraine’s underground gas storage facilities to strengthen regional energy security.

These developments are significant both regionally and internationally, particularly in the context of Azerbaijan’s relations with Russia.

In mid-July, Bayramov met Sergei Lavrov in Moscow and said the “difficult period” in bilateral relations was over and that ties had been fully normalised. A few weeks later, in Kyiv, he reaffirmed Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, while also signalling Baku’s interest in expanding energy cooperation.

The visit illustrates Baku’s multi-vector foreign policy. While maintaining dialogue with Russia, Azerbaijan has continued to provide humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and has expressed its readiness to support the country in the energy sector if required.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

Symbolic and practical significance of the Irpin visit

Irpin was one of the towns where the Russian advance on Kyiv was halted in 2022. Hundreds of civilians were killed during the fighting, and more than 70% of the town’s housing stock was destroyed.

Azerbaijan has contributed to Irpin’s reconstruction.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

The minister laid flowers at the bust of academician Zarifa Aliyeva in the park named after her, and visited the Zarifa Aliyeva Linguistic Lyceum and Irpin Central City Polyclinic, both rebuilt with Azerbaijan’s support. He was also briefed on future reconstruction projects, including plans to restore the town’s House of Culture.

In his statement, Zelensky said Bayramov had visited a school, a hospital and a rehabilitation centre supported by Azerbaijan. The visit to Irpin was seen as a demonstration of humanitarian solidarity with Ukraine, as well as Azerbaijan’s willingness to share its experience in rebuilding territories recovered from occupation.

I received Azerbaijan’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, @Bayramov_Jeyhun. This is the Minister’s first visit to Ukraine since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion. He began his visit in Irpin, where he visited a school, a hospital, and a rehabilitation center supported by… pic.twitter.com/7HTLIaz3EF — Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) August 6, 2026

The visit to a town devastated by Russian forces, together with Bayramov’s review of reconstruction efforts and Azerbaijan’s continued support, was seen as underscoring Baku’s intention to reaffirm its longstanding position despite the “normalisation” of relations with Moscow, particularly its commitment to the principle of territorial integrity.

Following the official welcoming ceremony at the Foreign Ministry, Bayramov and Sybiha viewed an exhibition of Ukrainian-made drones. They then laid a wreath at the Memorial to the Fallen Defenders of Ukraine and observed a moment of silence in their honour.

Meetings and gas supply pledge

During expanded talks with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, the two sides discussed their strategic partnership, trade, energy, transport, humanitarian cooperation and regional security. Bayramov reiterated the need for an early end to the fighting and a diplomatic settlement based on international law, while reaffirming Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders.

He said Azerbaijan’s total humanitarian assistance to Ukraine had exceeded 50 million US dollars. Bayramov also highlighted reconstruction projects in Irpin and rehabilitation programmes for children.

During his meeting with President Volodymyr Zelensky, the discussions focused on Russian attacks, the situation in the Black Sea, the disruption of grain export routes, defence cooperation, and cooperation in the energy, oil and gas, and agricultural sectors.

Zelensky thanked Azerbaijan for its energy and humanitarian assistance, as well as for maintaining constructive dialogue. Bayramov, in turn, spoke about the post-conflict situation in the South Caucasus and reconstruction efforts in the territories regained by Azerbaijan.

As part of his official visit to Ukraine 🇺🇦, FM of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 @Bayramov_Jeyhun visited the Embassy of Azerbaijan in Kyiv.



The Minister met with the Embassy staff and received a comprehensive briefing on the Mission’s activities. pic.twitter.com/UPqN5Hn9rx — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

At a joint press conference, particular attention was drawn to Bayramov’s remarks on possible gas supplies: “If the need arises, we will be ready to supply gas to our friendly Ukraine.”

He highlighted SOCAR’s long-standing presence on the Ukrainian market, as well as the importance of Ukraine’s underground gas storage system – the largest in Europe – for regional energy security.

The statement can be seen as signalling Azerbaijan’s willingness to contribute to the diversification of Ukraine’s energy supplies, while also supporting alternative routes for Caspian gas exports to Europe. Against the backdrop of Russia’s strikes on energy infrastructure in southern Ukraine, Baku’s offer also underscores the importance of competition and diversification in the energy sector.

During meetings with Kyrylo Budanov and Ihor Klymenko, the sides also discussed regional and international security, as well as prospects for energy cooperation. They reaffirmed their commitment to the principles of state sovereignty, territorial integrity and the inviolability of internationally recognised borders.

Expert: “Azerbaijan will continue to provide Ukraine with political, economic and humanitarian support”

lkhan Shahinoglu, head of the Atlas Research Centre and a political commentator considered close to the Azerbaijani authorities, wrote that the visit is being closely watched by Russia:

The Kremlin will closely monitor Jeyhun Bayramov’s meetings in Kyiv. Azerbaijan’s partnership with any country is an exclusive sovereign right, and no other state has the right to interfere in that process.

At the same time, Russia, which is waging a war of conquest against Ukraine, closely watches those who cooperate with Kyiv. President Ilham Aliyev‘s response to the same question from Ukrainian journalist Gordon, asked at the Shusha Global Media Forum two years in a row – that ‘Ukraine should not reconcile itself to occupation’ – angered chauvinistic circles in Russia. They believe Azerbaijan should accept the annexation of Crimea and the occupation of Ukrainian territories.

Just as Jeyhun Bayramov visited Moscow some time ago, he has now travelled to Kyiv. Ukraine is Azerbaijan’s partner, and Baku will continue to provide it with political, economic and humanitarian support.”

World.title: Giga Avaliani case: Two more arrested 10 months after Georgian teacher’s murder
World.content:
Two more arrested in Giga Avaliani murder case

Two more suspects have been identified in the high-profile murder case of a 28-year-old teacher in Georgia. On 5 August 2026, two teenage girls – Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili – were arrested.

Giga Avaliani, a mathematics teacher, was killed in October 2025. Five people have already been convicted over his murder, while the trial of a sixth defendant is still under way. With the arrest of the two girls, the total number of suspects in the case has risen to eight – all of them minors.

The arrests of Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili, after several convictions had already been secured, mark an unexpected and significant development in the Giga Avaliani case.

Nia Imnadze was one of Giga Avaliani’s former students and the girlfriend of the principal defendant, Aleksandre Gabashvili. Prosecutors accuse her of incitement to commit the crime.

According to local media, Anastasia Beruashvili is a friend of both Nia Imnadze and another convicted defendant, Giorgi Rikadze. She has been charged with failing to report the crime.

Giga Avaliani, a 28-year-old mathematics tutor, was returning home late on 1 October 2025 when he was attacked outside his apartment building. He fell into a coma following the assault and died on 24 October without regaining consciousness. Investigators say the attack was motivated by jealousy and what they describe as “unwanted communication with a girl”. The defendants have given a similar account. According to their version of events, Avaliani sent sexually explicit messages to his student Nia Imnadze, who told her boyfriend, prompting him to confront the teacher. Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, rejects that account. She says Nia had been skipping lessons and that Avaliani informed the girl’s mother, angering the student. According to Kupatadze, the attack was planned afterwards.

The Giga Avaliani case has become one of Georgia’s most high-profile criminal cases in recent years. Much of the public attention surrounding it has been driven by Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, who campaigned for what she said should be a thorough and impartial investigation. Her efforts also helped generate significant public pressure over the handling of the case.

From the outset, Kupatadze maintained that Nia Imnadze bore primary responsibility for what had happened and repeatedly called for her arrest. The recent detention of the two girls has therefore raised new questions.

But the key question remains: if prosecutors had sufficient evidence, why were the two girls not arrested earlier? Was their detention the result of new evidence, or did it come only after sustained public pressure and Eka Kupatadze’s campaign?

Detention of two girls

Both girls were arrested late on the night of 5 August, in what appeared to be coordinated operations. News of the arrests first emerged through a video of Nia Imnadze’s detention, which was released by her lawyer, Giorgi Lekishvili.

The footage is deeply distressing. It shows a large number of police officers arriving at Nia’s home. Her mother, visibly distressed, pounds on the front door, shouting: “Come in, all of you!”, “Maniacs!”, “Murderers!”, “Do you know that Niako is innocent?!”

The girl’s father, meanwhile, tells the police: “You are going to make me do something the whole of Georgia will be talking about. If you treat my child so unjustly, I will do it.”

Police officers try to calm the distraught parents.

“Why are you taking my child? On what grounds? What does the court order say?!” the mother asks.

“The lawyer has reviewed the court order,” one of the officers replies.

“Giorgi, on what grounds are they arresting her?” the mother asks the lawyer.

“On the basis of a court order containing only formal wording, nothing specific,” the lawyer replies.

Nia sits in the hallway on a sofa, curled up with her face buried in her hands. The video is being filmed by her lawyer, who occasionally strokes her hair.

Shortly after the video was released, reports began circulating on social media that the second girl, Anastasia Beruashvili, had also been detained. No footage of her arrest was made public, but the Ministry of Internal Affairs later confirmed that she had been taken into custody.

During her arrest, Nia Imnadze became unwell and was taken to hospital, where she spent the night. On 6 August, she was transferred to a pre-trial detention centre. Anastasia Beruashvili was also taken there.

Minors charged in Giga Avaliani's murder case in Georgia – read more Five people have already been convicted in connection with Giga Avaliani’s murder: Aleksandre Gabashvili – sentenced to 10 years and five months’ imprisonment. He was the principal defendant in the case and was found guilty of organising a group assault and intentionally inflicting grievous bodily harm as part of a group, resulting in the victim’s death. Giorgi Rikadze – sentenced to 10 years and five months’ imprisonment. A friend of Aleksandre Gabashvili, he was convicted on the same charges. Demetere Chikovani – sentenced to six years and nine months’ imprisonment. He was convicted of attempted intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm in the Avaliani case, as well as organising group violence in connection with the case and four other incidents. Ani Naskidashvili – sentenced to five years and three months’ imprisonment. She was found guilty of failing to report a particularly serious crime. Another minor – sentenced to three years’ imprisonment. He was convicted of giving false testimony. The nature of the false statements has not been disclosed. His case was heard behind closed doors, lawyers involved in the proceedings are bound by a non-disclosure order, and the teenager’s parents have declined to speak to the media. According to TV Pirveli, the boy is named Luka Klatkin. Giorgi Malania – arrested in July 2026 and charged with aiding and abetting the intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm committed by a group. Malania is the son of a former senior Interior Ministry official, who served as deputy interior minister between 2016 and 2019. His trial is still under way and no verdict has yet been delivered.

Eka Kupatadze’s reaction

“Georgia has won another battle against the killers of a healthy, innocent and talented young man – Giga Avaliani!” Eka Kupatadze said in response to the girls’ arrests.

Giga Avaliani’s family has always maintained that those who carried out the attack were not the only people involved. They have consistently called on investigators to identify and prosecute all those who may have played a role in the crime.

The family has paid particular attention to the alleged role of the two girls. Eka Kupatadze has repeatedly said that they knew the attack was being planned.

Until recently, however, prosecutors had taken no apparent action against additional suspects, prompting repeated criticism of the investigation from Avaliani’s family.

Kupatadze even appealed for help to Ekaterine Khvedelidze, the wife of Bidzina Ivanishvili, the founder of the ruling party and widely regarded as Georgia’s “informal ruler”. Khvedelidze replied to her letter, expressing sympathy and support for the mother who had lost her son.

“As far as I am aware, the investigation has not yet been completed. I am confident that the relevant state authorities will see it through to the end and that all the circumstances will be thoroughly examined, so that no question surrounding the terrible tragedy that has befallen you remains unanswered,” Ekaterine Khvedelidze wrote in her reply.

Formal charges

On the evening of 6 August, both girls were formally charged.

Nia Imnadze at the time of her arrest

Nia Imnadze has been charged with incitement to intentionally inflict grievous bodily harm committed by a group. The offence carries a maximum sentence of 13 years’ imprisonment.

Anastasia Beruashvili has been charged with failing to report a particularly serious crime, an offence punishable by up to seven years’ imprisonment.

Under Georgian law, sentences imposed on minors are reduced by one quarter.

“The investigation conducted by the Ministry of Internal Affairs under the supervision of the Prosecutor’s Office established that, in September 2025, Nia Imnadze began taking mathematics lessons with Giga Avaliani. The accused, Nia Imnadze, told her friends Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Malania that her teacher, Giga Avaliani, had allegedly shown her excessive attention. By doing so, the accused incited Aleksandre Gabashvili to attack Giga Avaliani together with his accomplices,” the Prosecutor’s Office said in a statement.

According to the statement, Aleksandre Gabashvili, together with Giorgi Rikadze, Giorgi Malania and Demetere Chikovani, “decided to act on that incitement.”

What defence says

The defence has denied all the charges.

According to Nia Imnadze’s lawyer, Giorgi Lekishvili, there is no evidence in the case to support the allegation that she incited the attack.

The lawyer also rejected reports that prosecutors had obtained data and messages from Meta, and that the arrests followed an examination of those materials.

“Criminal proceedings cannot be based on suspicion. They must be based on lawfully obtained evidence, and no other standard can override that principle,” Lekishvili told reporters.

Ketevan Vardanashvili, the lawyer representing Anastasia Beruashvili, made similar arguments. She said Anastasia had not witnessed any crime and that she and Nia Imnadze had seen each other only once, for a few minutes.

“They had no friendship and no contact,” the lawyer said.

As for Anastasia’s relationship with the convicted defendant Giorgi Rikadze, Vardanashvili said that “even if she was his girlfriend, that does not mean she had any knowledge of the crime.”

Complaint or incitement?

The arrests of the two girls have sparked intense debate on social media. Many commentators agree that everyone responsible for Giga Avaliani’s death should be held accountable and that justice should be served. Many have also expressed sympathy for Eka Kupatadze.

At the same time, some have questioned the actions of the law enforcement authorities. They have asked whether prosecutors have sufficiently strong evidence against the two girls, particularly Nia Imnadze, who faces a lengthy prison sentence if convicted.

The Prosecutor’s Office statement says only that Nia Imnadze told her friends that Giga Avaliani had allegedly shown her excessive attention. It does not explain whether she knew an attack was being planned or whether she urged her boyfriend to take any specific action.

“Does complaining to friends amount to incitement?” some social media users have asked.

Others have also questioned why, if prosecutors had sufficient evidence, the girls were arrested only 10 months after the murder. Some have asked whether the arrests were prompted by Eka Kupatadze’s campaign, and whether political influence may have played a role.

Those questions also remain unanswered.

Timeline of Giga Avaliani's case – read more 1 October 2025 – The attack

Giga Avaliani, a 28-year-old mathematics teacher, was attacked outside his home in Tbilisi. 24 October 2025 – Death

After spending 23 days in a coma, Giga Avaliani died. November–December 2025 – First arrests

Four minors were arrested: Aleksandre Gabashvili, Giorgi Rikadze, Demetere Chikovani and Ani Naskidashvili. April 2026 – First convictions

Tbilisi City Court found Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Rikadze guilty and sentenced each to 10 years and six months’ imprisonment. Demetere Chikovani was sentenced to six years and nine months’ imprisonment. He was later convicted over separate violent offences committed at a different time, increasing his total sentence to nine years and nine months. June 2026 – Another conviction

The court sentenced Ani Naskidashvili to five years and three months’ imprisonment for failing to report the crime. July 2026 – Another arrest

Giorgi Malania was arrested. According to prosecutors, he was charged with aiding and abetting the intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm committed by a group. His trial is still under way and no verdict has yet been delivered. August 2026 – Two more arrests

Two more minor girls were arrested: Nia Imnadze, Giga Avaliani’s former student and the girlfriend of the principal convicted defendant, and Anastasia Beruashvili, described as a friend of Nia Imnadze and the girlfriend of the second convicted defendant.

Broader picture

From the outset, the Giga Avaliani case came to represent more than a single criminal investigation.

It exposed a range of systemic problems, most notably a lack of public trust in investigative authorities. The case also highlighted shortcomings in Georgia’s juvenile justice system, as well as concerns over the protection of the rights of both victims and defendants.

Many observers questioned the release of footage showing Nia Imnadze’s arrest, particularly as it was made public by her lawyer. Some argued that the video was intended to generate public sympathy for his client.

“Unfortunately, public trust in the justice system – the police, the Prosecutor’s Office, the courts and other institutions – is now so low that victims, defendants and lawyers increasingly see shaping public opinion as the only way to obtain justice. They then seek to use public pressure to their advantage,” lawyer Londa Toloraia wrote.

In her view, this reflects a profound crisis affecting both citizens and the justice system itself.

“You no longer trust the state, even when it may actually be making a lawful decision.”

Toloraia also raised a number of questions about the arrests of the two girls: What evidence were they based on? Why did they take place 10 months after the murder? And why were they carried out at night, when Georgian law restricts procedural actions during nighttime hours, particularly in cases involving minors?

“How much influence does public opinion have over the justice system? A great deal. It is extremely difficult to withstand public pressure. And where institutions are fully politicised, it becomes virtually impossible to make a decision that is unpopular with the public,” she argued.

She stressed that legal standards must be upheld even when dealing with those accused of serious crimes – especially when the defendants are minors.

The Avaliani case has also exposed a darker side of public reaction. Following Nia Imnadze’s arrest, social media was flooded with hostile comments directed at both her and her family. Many users described her as the main culprit and called for severe punishment. Others went further, posting comments about the suffering they believed awaited her in prison.

A second group of social media users expressed concern about the tone of those comments. Toloraia addressed the debate in a lengthy social media post.

“Children are not born criminals. Before demanding that they be lynched, we should first ask why they became who they are,” she wrote, adding that juvenile crime in Georgia has reached one of its highest levels in recent years. She argued that the state’s response has focused on opening a “special prison” for children rather than preventing youth crime. A state in which parents who have lost a child must seek justice through public mobilisation, while institutions make decisions according to fluctuations in public pressure, is a broken state,” Toloraia concluded.

World.title: Children encountering extremism at 'disturbing' rate, inquiry told
World.content:
Children at an increasingly young age are engaging with violent extremist material at a "disturbing" rate, Australia's counter-terrorism coordinator says.

The Department of Home Affairs' Brendan Dowling was appointed counter-terrorism coordinator earlier this year after the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion recommended making the role full time.

Mr Dowling works in collaboration with federal, state and territory governments and law enforcement agencies to coordinate a nationally--consistent response to counter-terrorism and violent extremism threats.

The commission has previously heard children as young as 10 are eligible to be referred to voluntary countering violent extremism programs in some jurisdictions in response to current trends.

Mr Dowling says the trends are "disturbing". (ABC News: Liam Patrick)

Fronting the royal commission on Tuesday, Mr Dowling said this was consistent with Department of Home Affairs data.

"The trends are disturbing," he said.

"The rates of youth radicalisation … we see an increasing number of younger people engaging with extremist material.

"It's often across a range of ideologies … whether it be neo-Nazi material, white supremacist material, anti-government material, jihadi material."

Mr Dowling said the trends pointed to countering violent extremism programs as becoming "critically important" in addressing radicalisation in the community.

"When you are talking about a person at that [young], age a law enforcement response is sometimes going to be the right response but in many cases, a [countering violent extremism] intervention outside of the law enforcement domain might be a far more appropriate response for a child who is engaged in extremist material," he said.

Risk of violent extremist material 'very real'

The commission heard hundreds of people were referred to countering violent extremism programs each quarter, but a large proportion were assessed as better suited to other treatment and diversion initiatives such as those related to mental health interventions.

Mr Dowling said the Diversions Australia pilot program, which ran from January to May this year, was an example of how social media and gaming platforms could work alongside counter-terrorism agencies to disrupt a young person's progression to radicalisation.

"[Social media platforms] are a vector for people being able to reach violent extremist material," he said.

As part of the pilot, users who searched for or engaged with violent extremist content on TikTok were presented with a pop-up inviting them to connect with case managers who could help them disengage with that material and related ideologies.

The commission heard over the five-month pilot, more than 6,500 users connected to the pilot site and about 790 of those engaged with the pop-up.

The pilot ran on TikTok between January and May this year. (Reuters: Hollie Adams)

About 12 of those progressed to having conversations with case managers or practitioners.

Mr Dowling said the data was a "positive indicator of the reach of the program", which he said he believed was a world-first.

"While it might seem like a small number are then engaging more deeply, if those people are higher risk individuals, then those are positive indicators of the types of people that are being picked up through that service," he said.

"I'm not aware that this type of program has been tried anywhere else in the world.

"There is enough evidence there to indicate this is a worthwhile undertaking and that it is worth looking at expanding to further social media platforms."

Mr Dowling said there were discussions underway with Roblox to expand the program to the popular gaming service.

"We know that as a platform where there is a lot of user-generated content, the risk of violent extremist material or communications is very real," he said.

World.title: Brother of alleged Alan Jones victim only found out after arrest, court told
World.content:
The brother of a man accusing Alan Jones of indecent assault has told the court he never saw the radio host act inappropriately towards his brother, and was only told of the allegations after Mr Jones's arrest.

Complainant J, a former youth athlete who has alleged Mr Jones kissed and touched him indecently when he was 17 or 18, has finished giving evidence in Mr Jones's criminal trial in the New South Wales Local Court.

Mr Jones's lawyers have accused Complainant J of "concocting" his evidence based on other media reports.

The 85-year-old has pleaded not guilty to 20 counts of assault with act of indecency and two counts of sexual touching relating to six alleged victims between 2003 and 2020.

Complainant J's brother has been called as a witness, and told the court on Tuesday he recalls first meeting Mr Jones in 2003 through his brother, because Mr Jones was interested in his emerging sporting career.

He recalled seeing news of Mr Jones arrest in the media and gave evidence that Complainant J asked to meet him at a fast-food restaurant shortly after.

Alan Jones arrives at court with his legal team. (ABC News: Jamie McKinnell)

"He said to me, in relation to the defendant, 'This is the hardest thing I've ever had to tell you.'

"'You've probably seen the news about the defendant.

"'I'm one of the people who've come forward,'" the witness said Complainant J told him.

The witness said he asked his brother at the restaurant what Mr Jones had done to him.

He said his brother did not give too much detail about the alleged offending, but told him, "he didn't try to f*** me or anything like that".

"He would try … he would grab me on the c***, he'd kiss me," the witness said his brother told him.

He said he asked Complainant J on that day why he did not say anything at the time, and that Complainant J told him he did not want Mr Jones's money and support to stop.

The witness told the court he visited the broadcaster's studios and his Macquarie Street apartment on different occasions in 2003, around the time Complainant J has alleged the offending began.

Brother says he did not see Jones act inappropriately

Crown prosecutor Georgina Wright SC asked the witness, "Did you ever see the defendant act inappropriately towards your brother?"

"I didn't," he replied.

Alan Jones's trial kicks-off at Sydney's Downing Centre Alan Jones sat impassively, legs crossed, with a notebook and pen in hand as the first of six male complainants began testifying this week in his indecent assault trial.

Complainant J's brother told the court he recalled his brother getting a mobile phone and a car from Mr Jones, as well as weekly payments to help with his training.

He said he visited Mr Jones's Fitzroy Falls farmstay on one occasion, which the court has heard was on a different visit to the one where Complainant J alleges he was assaulted.

Mr Jones offered to help the Complainant J's brother with an engagement ring when he talked about plans to propose to his now wife, the court heard.

It is alleged the talkback host then gifted Complainant J's brother a Villeroy and Bosch dinner set for a wedding present.

Complainant J has previously told the court he felt "scared" of Mr Jones at the time of the alleged offending and has admitted not wanting his weekly payments from Mr Jones to stop.

World.title: Aussie open water swim queen Johnson triumphs at Pan Pacs
World.content:
Australia's world champion Moesha Johnson has continued her season of complete dominance in open water swimming, winning the Pan Pacific Championships 10-kilometre title off Long Beach, California.

Racing on the same waterfront expected to be used for the 2028 Olympics, 28-year-old Johnson grabbed the lead on the second of six laps and won comfortably in one hour 55 minutes and 33 seconds on Tuesday (AEST).

She finished more than 26 seconds clear of silver medallist Airi Ebina of Japan, with Ichika Kajimoto (Japan) third and fellow Australian Jacqueline Davison-McGovern fifth in the 23-strong field.

"I really wanted to win going into the race today, and it's a strong group of girls, they're really fit and everyone's in really good shape," Johnson said after the race.

Do you have a story idea about women in sport? Email us abcsport5050@your.abc.net.au

"Realistically I had to keep an eye on where my heart rate and my effort was sitting and Jacqui (Davison-McGovern) was there at my feet the whole way.

"I wanted to keep her with me but at the end I just wanted to make sure I had the gears to keep shifting [up].

ABC Sport Daily podcast ABC Sport Daily is your daily sports conversation. We dive into the biggest story of the day and get you up to speed with everything else that's making headlines.

"I really wanted to have a dominating race on American soil leading into LA '28.

"Even when I was well ahead at the end I just wanted to keep putting on a show for everyone."

The victory extended a dazzling 2026 campaign for Johnson, who won all four World Cup 10km races plus all four 3km races.

The 2024 Olympic silver medallist is a three-time world championship gold medallist, having won 5km and 10km last year in Singapore.

AAP/ABC

World.title: How Gianni Infantino's FIFA leadership imploded over two weeks
World.content:
Gianni Infantino's future as the head of FIFA will ultimately be decided by each of the organisation's 211 member nations.

Unless an emergency election — known as an Extraordinary Congress — is called, his leadership will be determined at the next Presidential Election at the FIFA Congress to be held in Morrocco on March 17, next year.

An Extraordinary Congress can only be called by the 37-member FIFA Council, or if 20 per cent of the 211 nations — 43 members — issue a written request that that one be held.

If that does not happen, presidential candidates expecting to run against Mr Infantino in March will need to be named by November 18.

According to FIFA's rules, each member nation has a single vote — regardless of size, population or influence and success in football.

FIFA presidents are allowed to remain as leader for three terms consecutively, but no longer.

Mr Infantino has already been re-elected twice consecutively after he ran unopposed in 2019 and 2023.

He also led for three years before that after he replaced Sepp Blatter amid FIFA's notorious corruption scandal, but those years were not considered as a complete presidential term.

Candidates who could run against Mr Infantino would need to be endorsed by at least five member nations.

If there is just a single opponent against Mr Infantino, the eventual victor would need to be elected with 50 per cent of the 211 votes.

If there are more than two candidates in the race, run-off votes are held to reduce the number to a final duo.

World.title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez open to presidential run, announces she will freeze eggs
World.content:
US congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez is freezing her eggs and says she will be documenting the process on her social media.

"It has taken me time to consider, weigh and save up for, and it is of a sensitive matter and a personal matter and usually I keep my private life quite private, but I have made the decision to start freezing my eggs," Ms Ocasio-Cortez said in a video posted to her Instagram stories over the weekend.

Ms Ocasio-Cortez shared a video showing her medications laid out on a table before filming herself doing what she said was the first injection in her egg freezing cycle.

"Don't be weird about this, even though I know all of you will be," she said while sanitising a patch of skin on her stomach to use as an injection site.

Being elected at a young age to represent New York's 14th district came with the flip side of having to "grow up in the public eye", Ms Ocasio-Cortez said.

Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez shared a video of herself injecting medications at a TV studio where she was being interviewed. (Supplied: Instagram)

The now 36-year-old was sworn into the US House of Representatives in 2019 when she was 29, making her the youngest woman ever to serve in the US Congress.

"This is a choice that I am making to feel more in control of my life and if people want to make assumptions about my decision, let them make those assumptions.

"I feel empowered to make this choice, I think it's a very privileged position that I've been able to make."

Presidential run not 'ruled out'

In an interview with US broadcaster ABC's program This Week, Ms Ocasio-Cortez said she was not ruling out a presidential run.

"I'm focused on winning the mid-terms. I'm running for Congress right now," Ms Ocasio-Cortez said in the interview on Sunday.

In Trump's America, the grief of losing a baby can be followed by handcuffs In the wake of widespread abortion bans, US prosecutors launch hundreds of cases charging people with crimes related to their pregnancy, miscarriage, stillbirth or birth.

"I haven't ruled out the possibility. And I'm very humbled to the tremendous amount of support out there."

In her earlier Instagram posts, Ms Ocasio-Cortez said she was aware her choice to share her egg-freezing process came with "political risk".

"I'm also aware that in all of this kind of swirling conversation that happens, I am now kind of now opening the door to this being part of that discussion," she said.

"This is just not something that men deal with."

"Men run for office or frankly they interview for jobs and people don't think in the back of their mind, 'okay, this guy's running for office, how old is he? Oh well, is he going to want to start a family?'"

Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez said she felt "empowered" by the decision to freeze her eggs. (Reuters: Al Drago, file)

She said US President Donald Trump's administration was "dedicated to politicising women's bodies and taking our choices away from us and punishing us around decision to be pregnant or not be pregnant."

" Frankly, this administration has made pregnancy more dangerous than probably at any point in the last 30+ years, we're going to take our power back and we have to talk about it. "

Mr Trump's first-term appointees to the US Supreme Court provided the margins that struck down the Roe v Wade decision in a 2022 ruling. Roe v Wade had established a constitutional right to terminate a pregnancy.

Mr Trump has dubbed himself the "father of IVF" and even vowed to make IVF cost-free, although his measures fell short of imposing a mandate on employers and insurance companies to cover IVF.

His support of IVF has been contentious for his voter base.

While the majority of Americans support IVF, some conservative Christians oppose it because it often involves the destruction of unused embryos.

How egg freezing works

An egg freezing cycle typically takes around two weeks, and involves daily medical injections and ultrasound monitoring to determine how the patient's body is responding to the medications and when to collect the eggs.

The patient will take a trigger injection to initiate the release of the eggs, and 36 hours later the eggs will be collected in a procedure under anaesthetic.

The eggs can be frozen indefinitely, although different legal limits apply across the Australian states and internationally, and used to create embryos for in vitro fertilisation (IVF) in the future.

Retrieved eggs are frozen in liquid nitrogen, with patients paying annual storage costs to clinics. (ABC News: Hugh Sando)

A woman's likelihood of having a baby using frozen eggs largely depends on how old she was when they were frozen, said Alex Polyakov, Associate Professor at the University of Melbourne and a fertility specialist.

"In younger women, if you freeze eggs, you sort of stop the timing in a sense. So, every egg would have the same potential as a fresh egg in an IVF cycle, but at the age of freezing," he said.

While women's fertility begins to decline after the age of 35, the physical ability to carry a pregnancy can remain much longer provided there were no other health issues, Dr Polyakov said.

"As women get older, more and more of the eggs are genetically abnormal, and that reduces the chance of pregnancy, and it reduces the chance of a live birth."

But freezing eggs, even if it's done at a young age, never guarantees a baby, Dr Polyakov noted.

"No matter how many eggs you freeze, it doesn't give you 100 per cent chance that you would actually have a baby," he says.

"It's possible to freeze 20 eggs and then when you try to use them none of them survive the thaw. Or you thaw them and they survive, but none of them fertilise and become embryos. Or they become embryos but none of them become good embryos. So, there is attrition at every step," he explained.

Nine out of 10 don't use their frozen eggs

Data from the Australian and New Zealand Assisted Reproduction Database in 2024 showed that the number of women freezing their eggs to preserve fertility had almost doubled in the previous three years.

A meta-analysis of 10 studies conducted between 1999 and 2020 showed only one in 10 patients returned to use eggs that they had frozen.

This doctor warns women not to 'jump into' egg freezing Celebrity endorsements and social media influencers are helping drive more women to freeze their eggs. But one doctor is warning young women to seriously consider the financial, physical and emotional toll.

The analysis found that when using eggs that were frozen before age 35, more than half the women achieved a live birth, while for women who froze their eggs over the age of 40, the likelihood of a live birth was about one in five.

But the data also showed that women who freeze their eggs when younger are less likely to return to use them, while those who freeze their eggs when they are older are more likely to want to use them — but have a lower chance of pregnancy.

It's a dichotomy Dr Polyakov is familiar with.

"The younger age of freezing makes you less likely to actually need those eggs, because younger women, when they freeze their eggs … there is a decent chance that they will find a partner and have babies naturally, so they won't need them," he said.

"On the other hand, if you do it when you're older, the success rate is much less, but you're more likely to use them."

In IVF treatment, embryos are created and grown in a petri dish from sperm and eggs. (AP Photo: Michael Wyke, file)

Some people don't return to use their eggs because they decide to forgo having children altogether for a variety of reasons.

An egg freezing cycle in Australia typically costs between $3000 and $6000, depending on the clinic and the medications used.

Some people need to undergo multiple cycles to get a number of eggs they are satisfied with.

On top of the cost of the cycle, there is the ongoing cost of storing the frozen eggs.

The 'egg-counter' test

When speaking of the cost of egg freezing, Ms Ocasio-Cortez indicated fertility checks were "a great small step" for those who are "on the fence" or "not sure about costs".

Experts say egg-timer test is being misused Women like Libby French are using the egg-timer test to make high-stakes decisions about their fertility, but experts say it's not a reliable predictor of reproduction potential.

"A great small step you can take that can really empower you is to get your fertility checked," she said.

"It's a little bit of blood work and an ultrasound, they will give you your follicle count and then some short time after that they will give you something known as an AMH level in your blood which … it's a general kind of ballpark around your fertility and it is so empowering to receive that information because you can make a choice based on you."

The AMH test measures the anti- Müllerian hormone, which gives an indication of a woman's ovarian reserves— but many experts stress the test is misleading and not accurate for measuring fertility.

The test could help a doctor estimate how many eggs could be collected in an IVF or egg retrieval cycle, Dr Polyakov said.

"It does not tell you what your chance of natural pregnancy is at any given time. It does not tell you when you will run out of eggs. It does not tell you how long you've got," Dr Polyakov says.

"There are plenty of women in their late 20s who have low AMH and get pregnant with no issues."

World.title: 'Seismic shift': Māori set to invest in First Nations projects under new deal
World.content:
Indigenous business groups hope an historic deal with one of the largest and wealthiest tribal authorities in Aotearoa New Zealand will bring much-needed investment in large-scale First Nations projects.

The investment partnership between federal government agency Indigenous Business Australia (IBA) and the Waikato-Tainui iwi (nation) was signed today in Sydney.

Under the deal, IBA will help Waikato-Tainui, which holds around $AU2 billion in assets, invest in projects developed with Traditional Owners, including in the resources and agriculture sectors.

IBA chair Darren Godwell, a proud descendant of the Kokoberren peoples, said the signing of the "letter of intent" between two Indigenous investment institutions was a "seismic shift" for self-determination in Australia.

"We've got Indigenous institutional capacity that's willing to mobilise investment at scale so that TOs [Traditional Owners] can participate in the biggest projects that are happening on their Country," he said.

"Once we ... extend this invitation out to Indigenous Australia, we think we're going to be swamped with demand and opportunities."

Darren Godwell and Tuku Morgan signed the agreement Tuesday morning. (Supplied: Joseph Mayers/IBA)

Waikato-Tainui Chairman Tuku Morgan was in Sydney for the signing and said it represented a "watershed moment".

"This is about trying to build a new era of relationships that promises cohesion, better synergy on the basis of shared values, shared cultural values, shared environmental values, and the ability to do business with each other," he said.

Mr Godwell said the Waikato-Tainui, already a big investor in New Zealand retail, residential, ports and agriculture projects, is looking to generate long-term commercial returns.

He said the iwi is also concerned about being too exposed to the New Zealand economy.

"They need to offset that risk by investing in other places, and what better place to invest than Australia."

IBA's Darren Godwell says the deal is a 'watershed moment' for economic self-determination. (Supplied: Indigenous Business Australia)

The IBA will work closely with the Waikato-Tainui to help ease the transition into Australia, he said.

"We're going to share our information, our market intelligence, and then our relationships directly with TOs."

A 'stepping stone' for more capital investment

While the successful projects are yet to be decided, early beneficiaries could be Indigenous stakes in ports or large-scale renewable projects, as well as industries such as mining, agriculture and botanicals.

Mr Godwell said Yindjibarndi WaterCo's recent agreement to acquire the Dampier Seawater Desalination Plant in the Pilbara from Rio Tinto and the WA government is one contender.

"A large-scale project like that is something that's a very serious proposition for an investment partnership like the one we're announcing."

Michael Woodley hopes the deal will prompt broader interest in First Nations investment opportunities. (ABC Pilbara: Alistair Bates)

CEO of the Yindjibarndi Group Michael Woodley said the new partnership was an example of First Nations people empowering each other across borders.

"It hasn't been something that First Nations have generally been successful (at) in the past," he said.

"The market as well … will obviously see this as a stepping-stone towards supporting First Nations with capital investment for our ideas."

Mr Woodley said he hoped it would open doors for more global First Nations institutions to do the same.

"Australia is one of the establishing frontiers for First Nations in terms of economic development, economic investment," he said.

"That could lead to something bigger and better in terms of how we unite around the globe."

Many Maori tribal authorities in New Zealand hold investment portfolios funded by historical Treaty of Waitangi settlements, with proceeds distributed to community projects such as social housing, health, environment and education.

"At the heart of what we do is, how do we build and ensure the ongoing prosperity of our people and at the same time, achieve the preservation and ongoing sustenance of the environment [and] keeping our culture alive, our language alive," Mr Morgan said.

The Waikato-Tainui is made up of 100,000 people, including around 15,000 who live in Australia, he said.

"They married into First Nations mobs across Australia. They are part of our family.

"Connecting and doing this high-level agreement is more than just doing business. This is family."

The agreement will be signed again in New Zealand at the annual celebration of the Māori Queen's coronation, expected to be attended by thousands of people next month.

World.title: Perhaps the answer to my dating woes is to simply tell people who I am
World.content:
Every time I rejoin Tinder or another dating site, I am faced with the dreaded questions of whether to include my disability in my profile.

Often, I omit the fact and only disclose it after a potential match gets to know me a little.

I would like to say I am still being authentic, but in truth I am not.

I am performing an edited version of myself; the socially acceptable one that platonic and romantic prospects seem to connect with.

It is as if, by only mentioning my interests and goals — l am a foodie, history and art buff, and lover of long conversations — I am using my dating app descriptions to scream: "Look, I am just like you. Don't put me in a box."

l sold my belongings and said goodbye to 'fantasy me' I was tired of trying to live up to an idealised version of myself. So, I decided to do something I had learnt from Marie Kondo: sort my wardrobe into what brought me joy and what didn't.

At other times, I do include it, a disclosure coming from a place of acceptance and tiredness. Tiredness from pretending that I don't have a disability, and after a long time desperately trying to follow the rules of what is "normal" in dating, that in hindsight were not actually written anywhere and enforced by no-one but me.

With this disclosure comes the dreaded, unspoken "please still like me" and the questioning of whether I have characterised my disability in an abled-body-friendly way (not too off-putting?). At the same time the alarm bells are ringing in the back of my mind: "Why am I self-editing to make myself palatable?"

I turned dating into a chore

I never get around to answering that question.

My disability is a part of who I am, but it's not the entirety of who I am. (Supplied: Vanessa Mbeve)

Instead, I start swiping away at potential matches with the alarms still ringing in the background. For every 20 l swipe on l come across a profile of a person with disability and recognise something of myself in their profiles, in their choice of words.

Within 30 minutes I have matches, and right out of the gate I am performing a version of myself while getting to know the other person. Presenting my positives and downplaying my disability as a minor thing. As if to say the essence of who I am is not enough, and that my disability is a point of shame.

Disclosure during the chatting phase is met with a few instant unmatches, dead-end conversations, and the odd forward question: "Does your disability prevent you from being sexually active?"

Sign up to the ABC Lifestyle newsletter Get a mid-week boost and receive easy recipes, wellbeing ideas, and home and garden tips in your inbox every Wednesday. You’ll also receive a monthly newsletter of our best recipes.

But the vast majority of potential matches I encounter largely seem OK with my disability.

And yet when I meet them in person, the performance continues. I show up in character — not as myself — trying to prove I am "normal" and more than my disability. Instead of saying, "this is who I am and this is where I am at."

Do you have a dating story you would like to share? We'd love to hear from you

I am so busy trying to make potential partners comfortable with my disability that I almost forget the more important questions, like "do I even like this person?".

I am brutally reminded of that reality by my sister. When I described a date as "OK," she answered bluntly, "I don't think you like that guy. Otherwise, you would say he's hot, cute, or something."

In an instant, I get that ugly sinking feeling that I have set myself up for failure again because somewhere along the way, I turned dating into a chore. I stopped asking whether I actually wanted someone, or what my end goal was (marriage, a one-night stand, or something else?) and instead became focused on whether I could convince them to want me.

Do I really need to appeal to everyone?

As a result, I end up doing the exact thing I am trying to avoid: harming others and, above all, myself. I disrespect myself, and in turn I disrespect others by not allowing people to see me and make their own informed decision.

And at end of it all, I am exhausted.

For me, dating apps have, in theory, made dating easier and more accessible in terms of being able to meet people. But of all the people I met, I was genuinely attracted to and compatible with only a handful. So do I really need to appeal to everyone?

I no longer worry about what others think of me Vanessa Mbeve spent more than a decade hiding away from the world, unhappy with the way cerebral palsy affected her. Now, at 26, she's breaking free from self-imposed shackles.

The best date I've had so far this year was with someone who did show up as themselves.

We talked for hours until we were the only people left in the bar, and the staff were desperately waiting for us to leave so they could go home.

Maybe trying to find the perfect words to explain myself is a futile endeavour. My disability is a fixture of who I am, but it is not the entirety of who I am, just like all the other things I include in my dating profile.

Perhaps the answer is not to find a better explanation, but to simply tell people who I am.

My name is Vanessa Mbeve, I am 27 I have cerebral palsy. I am addicted to Cheetos and my laptop. On a weekend you will find me out or blasting music in my house while scrolling on Reddit.

PS; Did I mention I'm single?

Vanessa Mbeve is a New South Wales-based writer with cerebral palsy. She is passionate about exploring social dynamics and sharing her unique perspectives through her writing.

World.title: Victoria's work-from-home laws delayed until July 2027
World.content:
The Victorian government's proposed work-from-home laws will be delayed for nearly 12 months, as premier Ben Carroll allows more time for consultation and amendments to the legislation.

The laws were first flagged by former premier Jacinta Allan last year, when she outlined plans to develop legal protections for employees who want to work at least two days a week from home.

Mr Carroll said he had informed both Victorian Chamber of Commerce and Industry chief executive Sally Curtain and Australian Industry Group head Tim Piper that the implementation of the laws would be delayed by almost a year.

"I've spoken with Sally Curtain this morning, and Tim Piper, and I've informed them that work-from-home will not proceed on the 1st of September," he said.

"It will proceed on the 1st of July, 2027."

Ben Carroll says debate on work-from-home legislation will be delayed to allow more time for consultation. (ABC News)

Mr Carroll said he supported working-from-home laws, but said the benefits had to be balanced against other priorities.

"It is good for working families," he said.

"Equally though, we need to make sure that our economy — everyone knows its a partnership between working families and the business community and the government."

He said he would listen to and consult on any "common-sense" amendments, but promised the legislation would pass before the November state election.

Business community welcomes delay, but calls for scrapping laws

The Victorian Chamber of Commerce and Industry welcomed the delay, warning the legislation posed a "profound risk" to the state's economy.

"The Victorian Chamber maintains that the Bill must be scrapped, as it is completely unnecessary, costly and burdensome for Victorian businesses," chamber chief executive Sally Curtain said.

"The premier has been in touch with us directly and has indicated he is willing to meet with us. We hope to persuade him to abandon this destructive course."

In an exclusive interview with the ABC last week, the premier said resetting his relationship with Victoria's businesses was one of his biggest priorities.

"I'll roll the red carpet out for them. I want to grow our economy. We've got the best workforce in the nation, the most skilled. This is my focus," he said.

"I think it's about a rhetorical reset, making sure that business knows I'm in their corner."

Business Council of Australia chief executive Bran Black said the government was taking "the first steps" in listening to the business community, but still argued for scrapping the legislation altogether.

"Already, Victoria has the highest unemployment rate in the country and the Victorian economy cannot afford another policy that drives investment and jobs away, which only hurts Victorians through lower living standards," Mr Black said.

Business leaders have called for work-from-home legislation to be scrapped altogether. (Adobe Stock)

Shadow Attorney-General James Newbury said the opposition had announced their proposed amendments to the work-from-home legislation.

Mr Newbury said while the opposition supported work-from-home laws, it wanted to see amendments made to ease a transition period.

"Rolling out a change of this nature within three weeks across an entire economy is difficult," he said.

"I think it's only reasonable that there's some understandable delay."

He said the opposition was also asking for amendments to remove the right of unions to enter the property of a person working from home.

World.title: Australia to give bird flu vaccines to native species most at risk
World.content:
Australia’s most vulnerable native birds will be vaccinated against the H5N1 flu sweeping the nation, but challenges remain in protecting the poultry industry to prevent egg shortages. Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said on Tuesday the government had acquired $2 million worth of vaccines to inoculate about 1500 native animals in captivity that are most at risk from the disease. Minister for Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry Julie Collins speaking at Parliament House, Canberra, on Tuesday morning. Alex Ellinghausen “We’ve been very clear that we cannot stop the H5 bird flu from spreading amongst wild birds, but we can take action to protect the species most at risk, and the vaccination is now part of that response,” Collins said. The escalation of the national response follows confirmation of the first mass casualty event last week and as deaths exceed 200. As the outbreak spreads, Collins said reporting would shift from counting dead birds to confirming major events and newly affected locations.



Collins said species would be prioritised for vaccination based on the needs of state and territory governments, which would announce which populations they would target in coming days. Environment Minister Murray Watt said wild birds may be vaccinated where possible, but doing so was difficult. “It does take two vaccination doses to vaccinate birds, and it is difficult enough to catch wild birds once, let alone twice,” Watt said. “The priority here is to vaccinate birds that are ... in our zoos and various other institutions.” Watt added that Australia had increased its populations of captive birds while bracing for the virus to hit as it spread around the globe.



Collins added the risk of the H5N1 strain to human health remained low and there was no evidence it had infected Australia’s poultry industry. “Overseas we have seen it spill over into agriculture, so we’re doing everything we can do to keep it out,” she said. Related Article Live

National News Live Australia news LIVE: Albanese tells Labor caucus he expects gambling bill to pass with Coalition support; Ministers back PM as scrutiny over ‘melons’ remark grows The government is examining whether vaccinating poultry is feasible, but a rollout would be complicated. Biosecurity measures, such as keeping poultry away from wild birds, will remain the first line of defence for farms, which are bracing for stock infections. “The vaccine itself is not 100 per cent protective,” Australia’s chief vet Beth Cookson said. “So even in flocks that are vaccinated, they can still have the virus introduced if their biosecurity is not keeping the infection out.”



She said infected birds would need to be killed even if vaccinated, and some countries had imposed restrictions on the export of vaccinated poultry. Cookson said the vaccine had been developed for poultry, and had been tested for efficacy and safety in different sizes and species of birds over 18 months. On the weekend, the first case of H5N1 bird flu in inland Australia was detected in western NSW, at the junction of the Murray and Darling rivers on the Victorian border. Experts say it is a sign the virus will spread rapidly across the continent. This strain has devastated wildlife populations overseas, leading to the deaths of millions of birds and mammals and first arrived in Australia in June from Antarctic seabirds. New AI cameras that watch swimmers for signs of struggling or distress are set to be trialled at public pools in Brisbane.

A jury has been discharged in a trial of a doctor accused of manslaughter after a woman gave birth at home and died of heavy blood loss.

Robyn Mary James, 67, had pleaded not guilty to the charge after Vicki Butler died the day she gave birth at her Ipswich home west of Brisbane.

Butler, 41, died as a result of a postpartum haemorrhage which she suffered between James’ arrival at 5am and when the doctor called an ambulance at 6.42am on December 27, 2017, the prosecution said.

Dr Robyn Mary James outside Brisbane Supreme Court. AAP

Photos retrieved from Butler’s phone showed she had given birth between 3.22am and 4.07am.

World.title: Alan Jones trial live updates: Brother of complainant ‘J’ gives evidence in former 2GB broadcaster’s alleged indecent assault, sexual touching trial
World.content:
Warning: Graphic content

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of day six of Alan Jones’ lengthy criminal trial on charges of indecent assault and sexual touching. Our reporters Clare Sibthorpe and Jacqueline Maley will be bringing you the latest from the courtroom today.

Last week, the NSW Local Court in Sydney’s historic Downing Centre court complex heard allegations that Jones indecently assaulted a young athlete, starting with unwanted kissing when the man was a teenager in year 12 in the early 2000s. Jones denies the claims.

Alan Jones outside the Downing Centre Local Court on Tuesday. Sam Mooy

Our live coverage was paused on Wednesday after Local Court Judge Glenn Walsh temporarily imposed a non-publication order on the cross-examination of the complainant, known as “J”, by Jones’ barrister, Gabrielle Bashir, SC. That order was lifted on Thursday afternoon.

“J”, now in his early 40s, denied under questioning by Bashir that he had a financial motive for making the allegations against Jones, and denied that they were a fabrication.

He has given evidence that Jones groped him as he drove the then-radio host to his Fitzroy Falls farm. “J” has also told the court that Jones had indecently assaulted him at the property after telling him to wear “a robe and nothing else”.

The complainant said he came forward to police after seeing reports about Jones’ arrest in November 2024 because he wanted justice.

Jones had supported the promising athlete financially, including paying him hundreds of dollars a week to focus on training and giving him a car and a mobile phone, the court heard.

Today, the man known as complainant “J” returns to the witness box for a sixth day. He will be re-examined by prosecutor Georgina Wright, SC, after his cross-examination concluded on Friday.

A man known as “C” will be the next complainant to give evidence.

Bashir asked “J” a series of questions about whether he read media reports containing similar allegations about Jones in 2023 before he spoke to police the following year. He said he did not.

The Crown alleges that Jones indecently assaulted or sexually touched six men between 2003 and 2020, and is seeking to prove 22 charges against him, including nine indecent assault charges against “J”.

The former broadcaster has emphatically denied wrongdoing, and Bashir said during her opening address to the court that the credibility and reliability of the complainants’ evidence would be tested.

“Rivalry, treachery, double-dealing, money, hatred, desperation, opportunism and more are all at the heart of this case,” Bashir said in her opening remarks to the court.

Support is available from the National Sexual Assault, Domestic Family Violence Counselling Service at 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732) or the Men’s Referral Service on 1300 766 491.

World.title: ‘First-world problem’: Why Wallabies star says Suaalii shouldn’t be pigeonholed
World.content:
SportRugby UnionWallabies ‘First-world problem’: Why Wallabies star says Suaalii shouldn’t be pigeonholed Nick Wright Updated August 11, 2026 — 12:41pm ,first published August 10, 2026 — 9:17pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Wallabies fullback Tom Wright believes versatility will prove both Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii and Australia’s greatest weapon, dismissing the notion the game’s $5 million man needed to be cemented in one position. Every pundit in rugby circles has had an opinion on where the former NRL star’s future must lie in the build-up to the 2027 Rugby World Cup, having been largely used in the centres but deployed at fullback for the Waratahs this year. In the latter stages of the Wallabies’ 35-32 triumph of Japan to launch a new era under coach Les Kiss, Suaalii was shifted from outside centre to the wing – the same position he began his rugby league career in, where his near two-metre tall physique made him a lethal aerial threat. Les Kiss speaks to Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii during a Wallabies training session. Getty Images Wright was asked in Brisbane if the 23-year-old’s long-term future rested in the flank or in the midfield, getting his hands on the ball more frequently.



“I think it depends what lens you want to put on it; if we leave it ambiguous they [our opposition] won’t know what we’re going to do, so that’s awesome. Being that talented is a first-world problem, for there to be so many opinions on it means he’s almost too good,” Wright said. Related Article Wallabies ‘Is this the end?’: Contract call twists fate for plagued Wallaby “Everyone has an opinion on someone who’s that talented and has brought so much good coverage to our game. I think the versatility we’ve got pretty much across the entire backline is something that potentially is a weapon for us, being able to change the point of attack. “I think ‘Su’ could jump in anywhere; you could mould him into an inside centre if you wanted, you could give him enough time to play five-eighth I think he’d jump at the opportunity to do that. “He’s going to be brilliant wherever we put him. There are so many opinions on it, so you can run with how you will, but he’s such a good player for us, and such a team-first guy – there’s no mention from him that he wants to do this, or doesn’t want to do this.”



While Wright conceded the victory against the Brave Blossoms was far from the polished performance the Wallabies had sought to put in place, he said there were signs Kiss’ philosophies would reap rewards between now and the World Cup. Since arriving at the Queensland Reds three years ago, Kiss has encouraged his players to trust their instincts and skill sets – pushing them to freely express themselves with the ball and backing their judgement. Loading That mentality led to five tries in sweltering Osaka conditions – the first three to outside backs Wright, Harry Potter and Max Jorgensen – but also yielded four unforced dropped balls between Wright, Aukuso-Suaalii and five-eighth Declan Meredith. However, Wright – speaking ahead of Saturday’s return bout with Japan in Townsville – remained undeterred, adamant the group would continue chancing their arm under Kiss’ tutelage, while continuing to develop an understanding of when to pull the trigger depending on the conditions.



“You want to be able to trust your instincts, you love having a coach and coaching staff from top to bottom who push that style of play as well. We speak about bringing the game back to how you grew up playing in the backyard, and that was all systems go,” Wright said. Related Article City life Rugby star on the family ties that bind him to Brisbane “You want to trust the first thing that comes into your mind, but understand we’re versing the best of the best in the world. To be able to think in the next five or 10 minutes what’s going to give us the best chance … finding that balance is probably what every team in world rugby is trying to chase. “The way the coaching staff here, directed by Les, give you that confidence to play what comes to mind, and then everyone getting on the same page and backing that first call, has been awesome.” Wallabies assistant coach Tom Donnelly also confirmed forward Tom Hooper would be available for selection, having overcome a shoulder injury suffered in last month’s loss to Ireland.



“He trained with his club team down in Canberra during the week and ticked off everything he needed to do to become available,” Donnelly said of the 25-year-old, who will join the Reds from Exeter in mid-2028 ahead of the 2029 Super Rugby campaign. “He’ll train with us fully this week.” The Hooper revelation came before lock Miles Amatosero was issued a three-match suspension, after the Foul Play Review Committee found him “guilty of dangerous play for a contrary charge into a ruck or maul” during the Japan clash. Loading The 24-year-old’s yellow card was later upgraded to red for his contact on Japan captain Warner Dearns, and the FPRC determined the act of foul play merited a mid-range entry point of six weeks. Amatosero’s foul play admission, his disciplinary history, experience and remorse led to a reduction in his suspension.



He was given permission to apply to take part in World Rugby’s Coaching Intervention Programme as a substitute for the final match of the sanction, which would make him available to take on Argentina on August 29. That has opened the door for Reds star Lukhan Salakaia-Loto to replace him, having been recalled into Kiss’ squad following his surprise omission from the group that took on Ireland, France and Italy under Joe Schmidt. World.title: Sarah Pound’s roasted cauliflower, chickpea and golden halloumi salad
World.content:
Step 1 Preheat the oven to 180C fan-forced (200C conventional). Line a large baking tray with foil.

Step 2 Place the cauliflower onto the prepared tray. Drizzle with 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, season well with salt and pepper and toss to coat. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until golden around the edges and tender. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool slightly.

Step 3 Spread the almonds onto a separate tray and roast in the oven for 5 minutes. Add the pine nuts to the same tray, toss to combine, and roast for a further 5-7 minutes until all the nuts are evenly golden. Set aside to cool.

Step 4 Meanwhile, make the dressing by whisking together the vinegar, mustard, maple syrup, olive oil, salt and pepper in a small bowl until well combined.
